Role Title: Finance Research Expert


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $30 - $60 per hour

Time per task: around 4 to 8 hours

Location: Remote, worldwide

You’ll need: Hands-on experience reading US SEC filings and familiarity with US GAAP

Your tasks: Write finance research questions with a verified, sourced answer, and check each one against what AI models answer


Scope of Work

You will work on questions about real US public companies. Each question points to information that sits in long filings or IR materials, or that requires comparing several of them to find the right answer.


  1. Write questions that require finding a specific figure in a 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, proxy statement, earnings release or investor presentation.
  2. Write questions where two documents show different numbers and the answer depends on knowing which one is correct (for example, original vs. restated figures, or adjusted vs. reported).
  3. Pay attention to period and document version: the right fiscal year, the right filing, the latest amended version.
  4. Test each question against current AI models and keep only the ones they answer incorrectly.
  5. Rewrite questions when the wording allows more than one valid answer.


What we’re looking for

Hands-on work with US filings in one of these backgrounds:

  1. Equity research or investment analysis (sell-side or buy-side) covering US companies.
  2. Investment banking or corporate development (M&A, equity capital markets), with experience in deal filings, prospectuses, ownership history and subsidiary structures.
  3. Credit or restructuring analysis, with experience in credit agreements, bond terms and bankruptcy filings.
  4. SEC reporting or audit (Big 4 audit, corporate reporting), with experience in restatements, footnotes and how figures change across filings.
  5. Corporate law or due diligence (securities law, KYC, investigations), with experience tracing entities, executives and related parties across records.


You should also be comfortable reading long filings, including footnotes and tables, and have clear written English.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply with your resume and a short profile.
  2. Complete the finance interview. It is a short conversation about your experience with US filings and financial reporting. You don’t need to prepare or write anything. Finishing it is what moves your application forward.
  3. Review. We check your experience against what the project needs.
  4. Onboarding and first task. If selected, you get the guidelines and start with an initial task, which is reviewed before you continue.

Role Title: Finance & Accounting Expert


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote, global


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: Up to $90/hour equivalent.

Time per task: ~10 hours per task

Engagement: Project-based — paid per approved task

Location: Fully remote — no geographic restrictions. Strong English required (B2 advanced or C1 minimum)

Next step: Complete the role-specific AI interview — it’s how your expertise gets in front of the client

Your tasks: Design realistic, multi-step finance and accounting tasks with objective criteria for grading the output



micro1 is engaging experienced finance and accounting practitioners to design the tasks that measure what AI systems can actually do. Your domain knowledge is what matters here — no prior AI experience required.


The work is to turn real finance workflows into benchmark tasks: realistic, difficult, and gradable against objective criteria. If you’ve built a review checklist, trained a junior analyst against a standard, or signed off on someone else’s workpapers, that’s the instinct this needs.


Scope of Work

  1. Design multi-step tasks drawn from real finance and accounting work — FP&A analysis, financial reporting, audit procedures, reconciliations — with realistic reference files and clear instructions.
  2. Define objective grading criteria so two qualified reviewers would reach the same verdict on the same output.
  3. Build tasks that require judgment rather than lookup: ones where the right answer depends on reading the materials correctly.
  4. Create or source the supporting materials each task needs: spreadsheets, GL extracts, financial statements, policy documents.
  5. Flag tasks that turn out to be ambiguous or ungradable instead of submitting them anyway.
  6. Deliver approved tasks on schedule and at the required quality level.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. 5+ years of hands-on responsibility in FP&A, financial reporting, audit, reconciliations, or accounting — direct ownership of the work, not supervisory-only or adjacent exposure.
  2. Experience creating or applying structured review standards: audit programs, review checklists, close checklists, grading rubrics, or training assessments.
  3. Strong Excel capability and comfort reasoning across multiple documents at once.
  4. CPA, CA, ACCA, CMA or equivalent is a plus, but not required.
  5. Strong written English.
  6. AI or LLM evaluation experience is a plus, but not required.



How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview — this is how we showcase your expertise to the client
  3. Profile review
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

Role Title: Inpatient Coder


Role Type: Contractor


Location: United States, Remote


micro1 is engaging Inpatient Coders to contribute to a valued project focused on enhancing inpatient clinical coding accuracy and data quality. In this role, you’ll apply your facility coding expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input.


Scope of Work

  1. Review clinical documentation for accuracy, completeness, and coding integrity.
  2. Evaluate AI-generated clinical notes and summaries against real-world documentation and coding standards.
  3. Validate alignment between clinical documentation and assigned codes.
  4. Write prompts that test how an AI handles real healthcare administrative work, including billing and coding, insurance and prior authorization, scheduling, and regulatory compliance.
  5. Correct the code/data when the model falls short, grounded in day-to-day operational experience.


Required Qualifications

  1. Active coding certification such as CIC, CCS or CPC.
  2. Inpatient ICD-10-CM coding experience, including DRG, MCC/CC, and POA concepts.
  3. Demonstrated expertise in reviewing and abstracting information from EMRs.
  4. Strong analytical skills and the ability to interpret complex clinical documentation.
  5. Availability of at least 10 hours per week.
  6. US-based.


Compensation Structure:


Compensation is task-based, meaning experts are paid per completed task that meets the project specifications. The average handling time (AHT) is approximately 1 hour per task, and the effective hourly rate will depend on the number of tasks completed and successfully signed off times the selected rate.

Role Title: Bankruptcy Attorney


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote, US-based only


micro1 is engaging Bankruptcy Attorneys to contribute their specialized legal expertise to a customer's innovative project. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.


Scope of Work

  1. Analyze, review, and annotate legal documents specific to bankruptcy law, providing expert feedback and substantive commentary.
  2. Draft sample motions, pleadings, and court filings reflecting common and complex scenarios in bankruptcy proceedings.
  3. Evaluate hypothetical legal scenarios and deliver well-reasoned written explanations and argumentation.
  4. Contribute to the creation of educational content and model training datasets relevant to bankruptcy practice.
  5. Assess model-generated legal answers for accuracy, clarity, and alignment with current U.S. bankruptcy law.
  6. Participate in written and verbal communications, ensuring precise, high-quality input for AI training purposes.
  7. Identify nuances and emerging trends in bankruptcy law that can enhance the project's quality and breadth.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Juris Doctor (JD) degree from an accredited U.S. law school.
  2. Active license to practice law in the United States, with a minimum of 3 and up to 10+ years of recent, hands-on bankruptcy law experience.
  3. Direct experience as an independent contributor on bankruptcy matters, including filings, court appearances, and advisory work.
  4. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to explain intricate legal concepts clearly and concisely.
  5. Judicial clerkship experience, particularly for a bankruptcy or federal judge (preferred).
  6. Experience teaching law (e.g., adjunct or guest lecturer) or creating legal instructional materials (preferred).
  7. Editorial experience with a legal journal or law review during law school (preferred).

Role Title: Competitive Data Scientist (Kaggle)

Pay: $60–$120/hour

Location: Global, fully remote

Job Type: Contractor (~15 hours per week)

Schedule: Flexible-you choose the hours and days you work, including weekends if desired


We're looking for data scientists, machine learning practitioners, and applied mathematics experts with competitve Data Science experience. (Kaggle, DrivenData, etc.)


You’ll draw on your competition experience, mathematical reasoning, and programming skills to create tasks that require more than a plausible answer. Each task should have a reproducible environment, a verified reference solution, and reliable checks for successful completion.


What You’ll Do

  1. Build reproducible environments, prepare relevant data and dependencies, and implement reference solutions.
  2. Develop tests and evaluation criteria that reliably distinguish correct solutions from incomplete or flawed approaches.
  3. Run coding agents against tasks, investigate their failures, and refine the tasks based on observed behavior.
  4. Identify implementation errors, flawed assumptions, data leakage, and other issues that affect correctness.
  5. Document task requirements, solution reasoning, and verification steps clearly.

What We’re Looking For

  1. Demonstrated experience in data science, ML, quantitative modeling, or relevant research competitions. (Kaggle, DrivenData, etc.)
  2. Strong problem-solving ability and a clear understanding of the methods you use.
  3. Practical programming ability sufficient to implement and verify your own solutions.


Relevant competition platforms include Kaggle, DrivenData, Zindi, AIcrowd, Numerai, DataSource.ai, and CodaLab/Codabench.

Huge Pluses

  1. Strong coding experience, particularly in Python, including testing, debugging, and working with unfamiliar code

Role Title: Senior Machinist / Construction & Field Ops Lead

Pay: $40–$60/hour

Location: Global, fully remote

Job Type: Contractor (~10 hours per week)

Schedule: Flexible—you can choose the hours and days you work, including weekends if desired as long as you're active


micro1 is engaging experienced Senior Machinists and Construction & Field Operations Leads to contribute to a dynamic customer project focused on technical drawing comprehension and field plan execution. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters. This opportunity is ideal for those who are passionate about elevating industry standards, enjoy sharing their knowledge, and excel in clear, articulate written and verbal communication.


Scope of Work

  1. Review and interpret advanced machining drawings and Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing (GD&T) specifications to provide detailed, real-world feedback.
  2. Analyze and comment on CNC setup and programming documentation, offering insights into best practices and troubleshooting common challenges.
  3. Evaluate construction plan sheets, identifying potential issues, missing information, or clarity improvements based on practical field experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. 10+ years of experience as a master machinist, construction superintendent, drilling engineer, mine planner, cabinetmaker, or fire officer, with a strong track record of interpreting technical drawings and field plans.
  2. Comprehensive understanding of US construction, fire, or mining codes and standards.
  3. Expertise in CNC programming, machining processes, and GD&T application.

Process

  1. Apply to the role and complete the screening questions.
  2. Complete an AI interview of approximately 20-30 minutes.
  3. Complete the hiring manager review.

Start Timeline & Availability

We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts who are ready to begin immediately. If selected, you will be expected to start your first task within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.

Role Title: Photo and Visual Editors


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $55 - $100 per hour

Location: Fully Remote, Worldwide

You’ll need: Professional experience selecting, editing or retouching images for publication, clients or brands

Your tasks: Review images, choose the best ones, correct technical problems and explain your decisions in writing

You’ll review and edit images and judge their quality, accuracy and fit for a purpose. This is a good fit if you work as a photo editor, picture editor, visual editor or retoucher and make decisions about which images to use and how to correct them.


Scope of Work

  1. Look at sets of images and pick the strongest one for a given purpose.
  2. Judge technical quality: exposure, focus, color, noise and cropping.
  3. Mark images that were altered in a way that changes what they show.
  4. Check that captions and descriptions match what the image actually shows.
  5. Write a short explanation for each decision so a reviewer can follow your reasoning.
  6. Correct or retouch images following a brief.


What we’re looking for

  1. Professional work as a photo editor, picture editor, visual editor, retoucher or photo producer.
  2. Daily use of professional tools such as Lightroom, Photoshop or Capture One.
  3. Experience delivering images to a real audience: print, web, social, broadcast or brand work.
  4. Comfort explaining why one image works and another doesn’t.
  5. Clear written English.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply with your resume and a short profile.
  2. Complete the editing interview. It is a short conversation about your experience with image selection and editing. You don’t need to prepare, look at anything or write anything. Finishing it is what moves your application forward.
  3. Review. We check your experience against what the project needs.
  4. Onboarding and first task. If selected, you get the guidelines and start with an initial task, which is reviewed before you continue.

Role Title: Student Loan Specialist

Role Type: Contractor

Location: United States (Remote)

Time Commitment: 15-25 hours/week, short-term project


micro1 is looking for Student Loan Specialists to help evaluate and improve AI systems on federal student loan topics. You’ll use your borrower counseling experience to check that questions sound like ones real borrowers would ask and that answers are correct and useful. Accuracy comes first. No AI experience required; your domain knowledge is what matters.


Scope of Work

  1. Review sample federal student loan questions, identifying and flagging those that do not reflect real-world borrower inquiries.
  2. Draft and refine rubrics that outline what constitutes accurate and comprehensive answers to repayment, forgiveness, and relief program topics, such as income-driven repayment (IDR) plans and Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF).
  3. Expand rubric coverage to include loan servicing challenges, deferment, forbearance, and default management scenarios.
  4. Evaluate AI-generated answers using your rubrics, thoroughly checking for inaccuracies, missing details, or outdated guidance.
  5. Provide concise, constructive written feedback to the project team asynchronously, supporting ongoing improvements to answer quality.
  6. Spot and communicate instances of incorrect guidance, ambiguous borrower communication, or problematic servicing advice.
  7. Collaborate with other experts as needed to ensure rubrics and feedback reflect current federal student loan practices.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. At least one year of direct experience advising borrowers on federal student loans in contexts such as nonprofit counseling, college/university financial aid offices, loan servicing, or default management.
  2. Demonstrated expertise with federal loan repayment strategies, income-driven repayment (IDR) plans, forgiveness programs (such as PSLF), deferment, forbearance, and default resolution.
  3. Practical knowledge of loan servicing operations, servicer-related challenges, and strategies for communicating with borrowers effectively.
  4. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to convey technical guidance clearly and efficiently.
  5. Experience reviewing or developing guidance documents, rubrics, or training materials in the student loan field.
  6. Comfort participating in a remote, asynchronous project and providing actionable, detailed input via digital platforms.
  7. US residency and familiarity with current federal student loan regulations and practices.

Role Title: STEM Expert – Chemistry & Computational Chemistry (PhD)


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote (Worldwide)


Job Summary: In this role, you’ll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input.


Key Responsibilities:

  1. Design, evaluate, and critique chemistry and computational chemistry problems, workflows, and reasoning chains to support AI benchmarking initiatives.
  2. Provide expert-level insights on reaction mechanisms, synthesis planning, spectroscopy analysis, molecular simulations, and electronic structure methods.
  3. Assess and optimize experimental protocols, simulation parameters, and software configurations for accuracy and reproducibility.
  4. Analyze chemical, spectroscopic, and simulation data and provide actionable recommendations.
  5. Leverage domain knowledge to guide the development and validation of chemistry-related AI models and tools.
  6. Communicate complex scientific concepts clearly, both in writing and verbally, to technical and non-technical collaborators.
  7. Document findings, methodologies, and best practices to ensure knowledge transfer across the customer’s team.


Areas of Expertise (we welcome applicants from any of the following):

  1. Organic synthesis & reaction mechanisms
  2. Inorganic & organometallic chemistry
  3. Physical & theoretical chemistry
  4. Analytical chemistry & spectroscopy
  5. Computational chemistry & molecular dynamics
  6. Cheminformatics & drug discovery
  7. Materials science & polymer chemistry


Required Skills and Qualifications:

  1. PhD in chemistry, computational chemistry, chemical biology, materials science, or a closely related field.
  2. Hands-on research lab experience, including wet lab experience for experimental subfields, or extensive simulation-heavy research for computational subfields.
  3. Deep expertise in at least one of the areas listed above.
  4. Professional written and spoken English (C1 or higher).
  5. Proficiency in Python and/or industry-standard tools in your subfield (e.g., Gaussian, ORCA, Psi4, GROMACS, LAMMPS, RDKit).
  6. Excellent quantitative, analytical, and scientific reasoning skills.
  7. Outstanding written and verbal communication abilities, with the ability to clearly document and explain technical concepts.
  8. Track record of rigorous scientific problem-solving in complex chemistry domains.


Preferred Qualifications:

  1. Academic experience (postdoc, research scientist, faculty, or equivalent), strongly preferred.
  2. Peer-reviewed publications, patents, or contributions to open-source scientific software.
  3. Experience with AI/ML-assisted chemistry workflows or benchmarking.
  4. Background in drug discovery, reaction prediction, or retrosynthesis.

Role Title: Digital Artist


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote - US only


micro1 is engaging Digital Artists to contribute their creative and technical expertise to a unique project focused on evaluating and enhancing AI-generated images. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input.   4. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with emphasis on descriptive and technical visual vocabulary.

Role Title: Vlogger (Insta360, DJI Osmo, GoPro MAX)


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is engaging 360° Video Recorders (Insta360 / GoPro MAX) to contribute to a customer's project by capturing immersive, high-quality footage with leading 360° camera equipment. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform.


We are looking for individuals to collect third-person video across several real-world capture types, including movement through changing environments, vehicle navigation, and animal-mounted POV recordings. Recordings should focus on continuous movement, changing scenery, and natural navigation through the environment.


Scope of Work

  1. Capture a diverse set of continuous video clips (minimum 60 seconds each) of everyday activities in a range of environments, including indoor, outdoor, and in-vehicle settings.
  2. Consistently utilize compatible 360° or wide-angle cameras (e.g., Insta360, DJI Osmo, GoPro MAX series) with at least 170° FOV and 720p resolution, ensuring stable, third-person perspective according to project standards.
  3. Implement appropriate mounting solutions, such as backpack or vehicle mounts, to maintain a clear third-person view where your entire body and surroundings are visible throughout each activity.
  4. Follow provided guidelines and instructions for camera placement, activity selection, and safety to ensure data consistency and collection integrity.
  5. Document, organize, and submit video files in accordance with project specifications, ensuring all deliverables meet technical and quality requirements.
  6. Communicate proactively and clearly in both written and verbal form regarding progress, questions, and any technical challenges.
  7. Adapt to occasional updates in collection tasks, environments, or technical requirements as defined by project needs.


Compatible camera examples include:

  1. Insta360 (Any model)
  2. DJI Osmo 360
  3. GoPro MAX, MAX2
  4. Other action or 360° cameras that meet the minimum 170° FOV and 720p requirements or support reframing.


Examples of compatible third-person mounting rigs include:

  1. Insta360 Third-Person Backpack Mount and other harness-mounted extension systems.
  2. Owning a compatible backpack or vehicle mount is a plus and may let you start collecting sooner.


Third-Person Camera Setup

  1. Mounted above and behind you
  2. Angled slightly downward
  3. Positioned far enough back to keep your entire body consistently visible
  4. Stable enough to maintain the required third-person perspective during normal movement


If using a camera with less than 360° FOV, the mounting setup must position the camera far enough away to keep your entire body in frame while also capturing the surrounding environment. Your full body should remain visible throughout normal movement without frequently leaving the frame.


Handheld selfie sticks, chest mounts, shoulder clips, and stationary tripods do not meet the required third-person perspective.


Expected Recording Tasks may include:

  1. Natural everyday activities
  2. Indoor and outdoor activities
  3. Walking and moving through different environments
  4. Vehicle navigation and driving-related recordings
  5. Other similar real-world activities provided in the collection instructions


For vehicle navigation tasks, the camera must be securely mounted to the vehicle.


Recording Requirements

  1. Capture a variety of activities and environments
  2. Each continuous clip must be at least 60 seconds long
  3. Record at a minimum resolution of 720p
  4. Follow the required camera position for each assigned task
  5. Keep the relevant activity and surrounding environment consistently visible
  6. Follow all provided recording and safety instructions
  7. Examples of the recording style we are after: [Link 1]

Role Title: Photography and Cinematography Expert

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $55 to $100 per hour

Location: Fully remote, worldwide

You’ll need: Professional experience shooting photo or video for clients, productions, publications or brands

Your tasks: Review photo and video work and briefs, judge technical quality, composition and brief match, and explain your decisions in writing


You’ll review photo and video work and judge it: what works, what doesn’t, and why. This is a good fit if you work as a photographer, cinematographer, director of photography or camera operator and make decisions about light, framing, camera settings and final delivery. You need professional experience shooting for clients, productions or publications, and clear written English.


Scope of Work

  1. Look at photos or video clips and judge which one is stronger for a given brief and audience.
  2. Check exposure, focus, color, framing, lens choice and camera movement.
  3. Flag technical problems that would show up later (noise, flicker, clipped highlights, wrong frame rate or format).
  4. Check that the work fits the brief and the intended use (print, web, social, broadcast, film).
  5. Write a short explanation for each decision so a reviewer can follow your reasoning.


What we’re looking for

  1. Professional work as a photographer, cinematographer, director of photography, camera operator or video producer.
  2. Experience with real jobs: briefs, shoot days, post-production and delivery to a client.
  3. Daily use of professional cameras and editing or grading tools such as Lightroom, Photoshop, DaVinci Resolve or Premiere.
  4. Comfort explaining why one shot works and another doesn’t.
  5. Clear written English.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply with your resume and a short profile.
  2. Complete the curation interview. It is a short conversation about your experience with exhibitions, collections and attribution. You don’t need to prepare, look at anything or write anything. Finishing it is what moves your application forward.
  3. Review. We check your experience against what the project needs.
  4. Onboarding and first task. If selected, you get the guidelines and start with an initial task, which is reviewed before you continue.

Role Title: Federal Budget Analyst


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote, US only


micro1 is engaging Federal Budget Analysts to contribute to a customer's project focused on budget formulation and execution within the federal sector. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input.


Scope of Work

  1. Create realistic training examples of federal budget justification materials, including narratives, exhibits, and supporting analyses.
  2. Write sample responses to OMB passback with clear, well-supported analysis, and annotate the reasoning behind each choice.

Role Title: Small/Medium Business – Robotics Data Collection Partner


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is looking for small to medium business owners who want to participate in a paid video data collection project for AI.


Your business would help collect real videos of normal work happening in your workplace. These videos will help train AI systems to better understand how people complete real-world tasks.


You do not need experience with AI. We are looking for business owners with active teams and real day-to-day work.


Who can participate

Your business may be a good fit if you:

  1. Are an owner, partner, or co-owner of a business in LATAM, the United States, or Canada
  2. Have at least 2 employees who can participate
  3. Have regular work activities that can be recorded safely
  4. Can have each participating employee record at least 10 hours of work
  5. Can get permission to record in the workplace
  6. Can make sure participating employees agree to be recorded
  7. Can start soon after a short onboarding call
  8. Employees will use their own iPhone or Android phone to record. Their phone must have an ultra-wide camera and the required motion sensors.


Businesses that may be a good fit

Examples include:

  1. Construction, HVAC, plumbing, electrical, painting, and renovation businesses
  2. Auto repair, equipment repair, and maintenance businesses
  3. Machine shops, fabrication shops, woodworking, and manufacturing businesses
  4. Warehouses, logistics, delivery, and fulfillment businesses
  5. Landscaping, cleaning, pest control, and property maintenance businesses
  6. Catering companies, bakeries, restaurants, and commercial kitchens
  7. Hardware stores, garden centers, greenhouses, and nurseries
  8. The best fit is a business where employees do different hands-on tasks throughout the day. Assembly-line or highly repetitive work is not a fit.


Privacy and consent

We take privacy seriously. Before recording starts, the business owner must make sure employees agree to participate and that the business has permission to record.

Participants should not record any sensitive information.


Payment

Businesses are paid based on the amount and quality of approved video data collected.


Requirements

  1. You own or help run a business in LATAM, the United States, or Canada
  2. You have at least 2 employees who can participate
  3. Each employee can record at least 10 hours weekly

Role Title: Junior Transactional Attorney


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Job Summary: We are seeking Junior Transactional Attorneys for a part-time role at the forefront of legal AI. This opportunity is for early-career lawyers who want to help shape how advanced AI is trained, evaluated, and applied in real-world legal work, especially those who have foundational experience with drafting, reviewing, and redlining within the tech field.

In this role, you will review, assess, and contribute to contract redlining workflows used to train and evaluate state-of-the-art AI models. Your work will directly improve how these systems identify risk and interpret contract language to create tools with improved precision and legal judgment.


Key Responsibilities:

  1. Perform simulated contract negotiations and redlining exercises.
  2. Review and assess AI responses to contract scenarios, providing feedback to improve model performance and output precision.
  3. Apply objective evaluation frameworks and grading criteria to assess AI performance on contract tasks with rigor and consistency.
  4. Collaborate with product and research teams to refine data, guidelines, and best practices for AI-driven contract review solutions.


Required Skills and Qualifications:

  1. 1–3 years of experience (in-house or law firm) focused on transactional work, with exposure to agreements such as MSAs and NDAs.
  2. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with meticulous attention to detail.
  3. Strong analytical capabilities and ability to translate legal knowledge into actionable feedback for AI systems.
  4. Demonstrated interest in innovation at the intersection of law and technology.
  5. Ability to work with cross-disciplinary teams in fast-paced environments.


Preferred Qualifications:

  1. Prior exposure to AI, legal tech, or training initiatives.
  2. Experience or internship at a corporate law firm, ideally touching M&A or fund formation work.


Why Join:

  1. This is an opportunity to work at the intersection of law and technology.
  2. You will help define how AI is developed for a new generation of legal practitioners.
  3. You will build your experience in a high-impact research environment.

Role Title: Law Review Cite-Checker


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot


Pay: $50–80/hour

You’ll need: Current or recent law school enrollment, hands-on Bluebook experience, and law journal or law review editing experience

Your tasks: Review citation-checking rubrics and build sample cite-checking tasks


Job Description

micro1 is engaging law students and recent law graduates with law journal experience to support a legal citation project. If you’ve spent time cite-checking for a law review or journal, this is that skill applied to a new context. No prior AI experience is required — your Bluebook fluency and editorial judgment are what matter.


Scope of Work

  1. Review existing Bluebook and pincite grading rubrics, and flag rules that are unclear, incomplete, or would be applied inconsistently by different editors.
  2. Identify edge cases the rubrics don’t currently cover and recommend how they should be handled.
  3. Create sample cite-checking tasks: source material paired with citations containing realistic errors, along with the correct answer and an explanation of the rule involved.
  4. Build tasks across a range of citation types and difficulty levels, from straightforward formatting errors to subtle pincite and source-support problems.
  5. Apply Bluebook rules consistently across all submissions.
  6. Flag ambiguous cases to project coordinators instead of resolving them silently.
  7. Deliver assigned work on schedule and at the required quality level.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Current law student (2L, 3L) or recent JD graduate.
  2. Law review or law journal experience, ideally including a cite-checking or source-collection role.
  3. Strong working knowledge of The Bluebook, including pincites, short forms, signals, and parentheticals.
  4. Able to explain why a citation is wrong, not just that it is — the reasoning matters as much as the correction.
  5. Careful and consistent across long sessions of detailed review work.
  6. Comfortable working independently and meeting deadlines without close supervision.
  7. Experience as a journal editor, articles editor, or executive editor is a plus.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview— this is how we showcase your skills to the client
  3. Profile review by the hiring team
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

Role Title: Data & Charts Expert


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote, global


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $25-50/hour

Weekly commitment: Flexible — work on your own schedule

Location: Fully remote, global

Your tasks: Pick charts from your field, write questions about them, and explain the right answer


micro1 is looking for people who read charts for a living. Your job is to turn them into questions that test whether an AI can actually interpret data — and then explain the correct answer step by step.


If you work with graphs, plots, or dashboards in your field, you already have what this needs. No AI experience required.


We’re especially interested in people from:

Medicine & biostatistics · Finance & economics · Engineering & physics · Earth sciences & GIS · Data science & statistics · Operations & manufacturing


What you’ll do

  1. Choose charts from your own field — the kind you’d actually see in a paper, report, or dashboard.
  2. Write questions that require real reasoning to answer: calculations, comparisons, reading a trend, combining two series.
  3. Give the correct answer, and walk through how you got there.
  4. Use the right terms for what you’re describing: axes, scales, units, legends, error bars, time periods.
  5. Flag a chart or question that turns out to be ambiguous instead of submitting it anyway.


What we’re looking for

  1. Two or more years working with charts and quantitative data — professionally, academically, or in research.
  2. A degree in a quantitative or technical field, or equivalent hands-on experience.
  3. Comfortable with charts that have several data series, annotations, or statistical features.
  4. Able to explain a calculation clearly in English, in writing.
  5. Experience writing exam questions, assessments, or analytical exercises is a plus, but not required.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview for this role — it’s how your expertise gets in front of the client
  3. Profile review
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

Contract type Contractor

Project: AI image evaluation


About the opportunity

micro1 is looking for AI Photo Raters to support a customer project focused on evaluating AI-generated images.


In this role, you'll use your visual judgment to compare original photographs with AI-generated versions, identify inconsistencies, and provide detailed written feedback. Your observations will help evaluate image quality and support the refinement of AI models.


We're looking for people with a strong eye for detail and an understanding of photography, visual design, or image editing. Prior experience working with AI is not required.


What you'll do

- Upload original photographs for use in structured image evaluation tasks.

- Compare real photographs with AI-generated images to identify visual differences, inconsistencies, and artifacts.

- Evaluate details such as lighting, perspective, anatomy, textures, and rendering quality.

- Document your findings through clear, specific written feedback that explains what looks incorrect and why.

- Apply your knowledge of photography and image editing to assess visual accuracy and image quality.

- Handle submitted images and project materials with appropriate privacy and confidentiality.

- Collaborate remotely with other contributors to address project goals and evaluation challenges.


Qualifications


Required skills

- Strong attention to visual detail and the ability to recognize subtle differences between images.

- Clear written English communication skills, including the ability to explain visual observations accurately.

- Critical thinking skills and the ability to provide constructive, evidence-based feedback.


Preferred qualifications

- Experience or expertise in digital photography, image editing, graphic design, or related visual arts.

- Familiarity with image editing software such as Adobe Photoshop, Lightroom, or GIMP.

- Experience with AI image generation tools, image comparison, or visual evaluation projects.

- Ability to collaborate with others and communicate feedback constructively.

This is a remote contractor opportunity for candidates based in the United States. The work involves submitting photographs, evaluating AI-generated images, and providing written feedback according to project requirements.

Role Title: Tax Preparer, Individual Income Tax (Form 1040), TY2025 (EA/CPA)


Role Type: Contractor


Location: US, Remote


micro1 is engaging Enrolled Agents and CPAs who actively prepare individual returns to participate in a project supporting a customer. In this role, you’ll apply your hands-on preparation expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required. Your domain knowledge is what matters.


Scope of Work

  1. Prepare complete federal individual returns (Form 1040) from scratch under TY2025 rules, working through the worksheets, phase-outs, limitations, and carryovers by hand.
  2. Write clear, concise preparer notes explaining how each figure on the return was derived, so that every number can be traced and reproduced.
  3. Build realistic, self-contained tax scenarios involving complex returns, including self-employment, partnership and S-corporation K-1s, investments, and credits, specifying facts, dates, filing status, and expected results.
  4. Review and evaluate AI-generated returns and computations for accuracy and completeness, flagging errors by severity (critical, secondary, minor).
  5. Identify ambiguities, exceptions, and conflicts in the law or IRS guidance, and document them in structured written feedback within the digital review platform.
  6. Experts and Adjudicators: strengthen and audit scenarios and reviews, and resolve disputed outcomes (see levels below).


Required Qualifications (all levels)

  1. Active EA or CPA who currently prepares individual (1040) returns.
  2. 3+ tax seasons on complex returns (Schedule C, K-1s, investments, credits), not mainly W-2 returns.
  3. Fluency in TY2025 rules.
  4. Ability to compute a full return by hand (worksheets, phase-outs, carryovers) and explain each number in clear written notes.
  5. Strong written communication, with an emphasis on clarity, objectivity, and reproducibility.


Levels

  1. Contributor: Meets the required qualifications above.
  2. Expert: 5+ tax seasons. Able to audit and strengthen scenarios, making a task harder without making it vague. Trainer, reviewer, or QC background preferred. A careful, independent preparer who builds the return from scratch.
  3. Adjudicator: 10+ years with review or sign-off responsibility. IRS exam, representation, or QC partner background preferred.


Preferred Experience (specialty areas)

  1. Foreign tax credit and K-1 reporting
  2. Small business: Schedule C, Section 179, QBI deduction
  3. Investments and capital gains
  4. Energy and education credits

Role Title: Military Writing Specialist


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote (US Only)


micro1 is engaging Military Writing Specialists to support a unique project, leveraging expertise in military writing and reporting. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters. Contributors will use their background in Department of War (Department of Defense) documentation to generate, review, and evaluate a wide range of reports, summaries, and status updates reflective of authentic military processes. Your input will help develop benchmarks and grading guidelines that will teach AI to understand and replicate effective, compliant government communication.


Scope of Work

  1. Create realistic military and federal status reports, summaries, and executive updates based on prompts and supplied artifacts.
  2. Develop “golden responses” that demonstrate high-quality, standards-aligned reporting for use in AI model training.
  3. Draft grading rubrics and guidelines that reflect best practices in federal and military writing assessment.
  4. Evaluate AI-generated reports, providing detailed feedback in both written and verbal form.
  5. Share context on stylistic differences and individual approaches to common military documents (e.g., WARs, SITREPs, AARs, executive summaries).
  6. Produce supporting documents such as decision briefs, memoranda, and action officer updates when required.
  7. Collaborate with other subject matter experts to ensure diversity of reporting styles and adherence to branch-specific terminology.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Former U.S. Department of War (Department of Defense) professional with at least 3 years of relevant experience.
  2. Experience producing templated and standard reports such as Weekly Activity Reports (WARs), Situation Reports (SITREPs), After-Action Reviews, or similar artifacts.
  3. Expertise spanning two or more branches of the U.S. military is a plus; a diverse background across roles is highly valued.
  4. Proven proficiency in written and verbal communication, particularly in conveying technical or operational subject matter.
  5. Demonstrated ability to craft, grade, and review back office documents, PowerPoints, memos, and spreadsheets for military or federal purposes.
  6. US-based contributor with broad familiarity with federal documentation standards and compliance best practices.
  7. Comfortable collaborating remotely and sharing insights on nuanced, highly procedural reporting tasks.

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote - US/Canada preferred; UK and Latin America also considered

Pay: $60-120/hr. Paid per task

Time commitment: 10+ hours/week required; 20+ preferred.

Time per task: Approximately 3 hours, following approximately 15 hours of initial environment development. Estimates include agent execution time.

Your tasks: Build realistic transaction environments and use AI agents to create and review valuation models, deal materials, task instructions, and objective evaluation criteria.

micro1 is engaging experienced investment banking and M&A professionals to help build tasks that measure how effectively AI systems can perform complex transaction work.

You’ll turn live-deal workflows into realistic scenarios, supporting files, and client-facing deliverables. Hands-on experience with agentic AI tools is required: you’ll work with agents to develop the materials and independently verify their quality.

Scope of Work

  1. Build realistic transaction environments containing company information, financial statements, diligence materials, and deal context.
  2. Design multi-step tasks involving valuation, comparable-company analysis, financial modeling, and sell-side advisory.
  3. Use agentic AI tools to develop and review CIMs, pitch books, valuation models, and supporting deliverables.

Required Qualifications

  1. 5+ years of professional experience in investment banking, M&A, or sell-side advisory.
  2. Hands-on experience building valuation models, comparable-company analyses, CIMs, pitch books, and client-facing materials for live deals.
  3. Hands-on experience using agentic AI tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or Claude Cowork for substantive work. General chatbot use alone is insufficient.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Corporate carve-out experience — strongly preferred.
  2. Experience at a top-tier investment bank or M&A advisory firm.
  3. Industrials sector experience.
  4. Experience developing review standards, training junior professionals, or writing internal playbooks.
  5. Prior benchmark development or AI evaluation experience.
  6. Availability for 20+ hours per week.

How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions.
  2. Complete the AI interview — this is how we showcase your expertise to the client.
  3. Profile review.
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up.

Job Title: Computational Biology & Bioinformatics Expert (PhD)


Job Type: Contractor


Location: Remote (Worldwide)


Job Summary: In this role, you’ll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input.


Key Responsibilities:

  1. Design, evaluate, and critique bioinformatics and computational biology workflows to support AI benchmarking initiatives.
  2. Provide expert-level insights on genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic data analysis pipelines.
  3. Assess and optimize pipeline parameters, tool configurations, and statistical methods for accuracy and reproducibility.
  4. Analyze biological datasets (e.g., NGS, RNA-seq, variant calling, protein structure) and provide actionable recommendations.
  5. Leverage domain knowledge to guide the development and validation of biology-related AI models and tools.
  6. Communicate complex scientific concepts clearly, both in writing and verbally, to technical and non-technical collaborators.
  7. Document findings, methodologies, and best practices to ensure knowledge transfer across the customer’s team.


Required Skills and Qualifications:

  1. PhD in bioinformatics, computational biology, genomics, or a closely related field, or equivalent industry/research experience.
  2. Professional written and spoken English (C1 or higher).
  3. Hands-on experience analyzing biological data (e.g., NGS, RNA-seq, variant analysis).
  4. Proficiency in Python and/or R for scientific analysis, plus experience with standard bioinformatics tools (e.g., BLAST, samtools, GATK, Bioconductor, Biopython).
  5. Experience building reproducible workflows with tools such as Nextflow or Snakemake, and comfort working in Linux/command-line environments.
  6. Strong statistical, quantitative, and analytical reasoning skills.
  7. Outstanding written and verbal communication abilities, with the ability to clearly document and explain technical concepts.
  8. Track record of rigorous scientific problem-solving in complex biological domains.


Preferred Qualifications:

  1. Experience with AI/ML-assisted biology workflows or benchmarking.
  2. Peer-reviewed publications, patents, or contributions to open-source bioinformatics software.
  3. Background in single-cell analysis, structural biology, proteomics, or drug discovery.
  4. prediction/retrosynthesis.

Role Title: AI Jailbreak & Prompt-Injection Security Expert


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is engaging AI Jailbreak & Prompt-Injection Security Experts to contribute to a cutting-edge customer initiative focused on AI safety and robustness. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.


Scope of Work

  1. Design and implement advanced methodologies for evaluating AI system safety, focusing on ethical jailbreaks, LLM red teaming, prompt injection, and tool-use abuse scenarios.
  2. Create comprehensive cross-domain elicitation strategies to uncover multi-turn and complex adversarial bypass patterns in AI models.
  3. Develop, maintain, and update regression test suites that systematically test for jailbreak susceptibility and prompt-injection vulnerabilities.
  4. Construct robust evaluation frameworks that stress-test AI models against real-world adversarial threats, aiming to enhance overall system robustness.
  5. Collaborate with technical stakeholders to translate security findings into actionable improvements for model safety and risk mitigation.
  6. Document methodologies, findings, and best practices in clear, well-structured written reports and presentations for both technical and non-technical audiences.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. 2+ years of expertise in adversarial machine learning, LLM red teaming, AI safety evaluation, or a closely related security domain
  2. Proven experience researching, testing, or uncovering vulnerabilities related to ethical jailbreaks, prompt injection, tool-use abuse, or adversarial AI attacks.
  3. Advanced degree (PhD, MS) in computer science, cybersecurity, machine learning, or a relevant discipline, or equivalent operational/professional background.
  4. High credibility and recognition within the AI security or adversarial ML community—such as published research, open-source tools, or conference presentations.
  5. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with a strong focus on clear documentation and collaborative problem-solving.
  6. Prior participation in multi-disciplinary projects or cross-functional AI safety initiatives is a plus.
  7. Familiarity with current LLM architectures, prompt engineering techniques, and security assessment tools is highly desirable.

Role Title: Revenue Operations Specialist (SaaS)


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote - U.S. or Canada only


Opportunity Snapshot


Pay: $50–100/hour

Project kickoff: Already active — we’re onboarding candidates now

Location: Remote — U.S. or Canada only

You’ll need: Hands-on configuration experience in a CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot, or similar) plus at least two connected tools — billing, CPQ, ticketing, or project tracking

Your tasks: Work through realistic SaaS revenue operations scenarios and explain the reasoning behind your decisions



micro1 is engaging Revenue Operations Specialists to contribute to a customer’s AI training initiative. Your domain knowledge is what matters here — no prior AI experience required.


We’re looking for people who have personally owned the systems behind revenue and customer motions, whether under revenue ops, sales ops, CS ops, or implementation. The work rewards operational judgment: knowing which rule wins when two policies conflict, and what to leave alone.


Scope of Work

  1. Work through realistic revenue operations scenarios — CRM data models, process design, configuration tradeoffs — and explain the reasoning behind each choice.
  2. Resolve conflicts between operational policies: which rule takes precedence, why, and what you would deliberately leave unchanged.
  3. Design workflows that hold up under compliance constraints like approvals, access controls, and audit requirements.
  4. Diagnose revenue data problems — duplicates, broken lifecycle states, inconsistent metric definitions — and explain how you’d find the root cause and prevent recurrence.
  5. Flag ambiguous or underspecified scenarios instead of resolving them silently.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. 4+ years hands-on in SaaS revenue, sales, CS, or implementation operations — not adjacent or management-only exposure.
  2. Direct CRM ownership (Salesforce, HubSpot, or similar) with configuration experience, plus two or more connected tools: billing, CPQ, ticketing, or project tracking.
  3. Track record of resolving policy conflicts and explaining tradeoffs, ideally in fintech, healthtech, insurtech, or complex multi-product environments.
  4. Able to explain your reasoning clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview (30 minutes at most) — this is how we showcase your expertise to the client
  3. Profile review
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

Role Title: Corporate Attorney (BigLaw Firms)


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is engaging Corporate Attorneys from top BigLaw firms to participate in a unique project for a leading customer. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters. This opportunity is ideal for legal professionals well-versed in high-stakes corporate matters and interested in contributing to the future of legal technology.


Scope of Work

  1. Review and analyze complex corporate documents, contracts, and deal structures relating to mergers & acquisitions, private equity, and capital markets.
  2. Provide accurate, detailed input on nuanced legal scenario assessments to inform AI model training.
  3. Evaluate commercial litigation materials, identifying critical legal principles and procedural details.
  4. Deliver expert feedback on legal reasoning, issue spotting, and drafting approaches as part of project deliverables.
  5. Support the creation and refinement of legal data sets by annotating, categorizing, and explaining key issues in corporate law.
  6. Ensure all work meets high standards for accuracy, clarity, and compliance with US legal practice.
  7. Collaborate asynchronously with project managers and internal reviewers to align on rubrics and quality expectations.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Active license to practice law in the United States.
  2. Recent experience (current or within the last 3 years) at a top-tier BigLaw firm, focusing on corporate law, mergers & acquisitions, private equity, or capital markets.
  3. Demonstrated expertise in commercial litigation and high-value transactional matters.
  4. Exceptional attention to detail in the analysis and interpretation of legal documents.
  5. Experience drafting, reviewing, and negotiating complex agreements and legal instruments.
  6. Strong written communication skills, with the ability to clearly and concisely explain legal concepts for diverse audiences.
  7. Prior experience with legal data annotation or rubric-based review is a plus, but not required.

Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote, US-based only.


micro1 is engaging Compliance Attorneys to participate in a dynamic project for a valued customer. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Scope of Work

  1. Analyze, review, and annotate legal documents and compliance materials to inform AI system development.
  2. Draft detailed explanations, rationales, and responses to complex compliance scenarios, enhancing machine learning data sets.
  3. Evaluate and critique AI-generated legal outputs for accuracy, logic, and adherence to U.S. compliance standards.
  4. Collaborate remotely with project leads and technical specialists to provide expertise on nuanced compliance and regulatory questions.
  5. Develop scenario-based questions and answers reflecting current trends and challenges in compliance law.
  6. Identify ambiguities or potential legal pitfalls in AI outputs and suggest improvements for clarity and precision.
  7. Contribute feedback on process enhancements, supporting the continuous refinement of AI training protocols.

  1. Juris Doctor (JD) degree from an accredited U.S. law school and active attorney license in good standing.
  2. 3-10+ years of recent, substantive experience practicing compliance law within the United States.
  3. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to articulate complex concepts clearly and concisely.
  4. US-based, currently practicing in the field of compliance law.
  5. Judicial clerkship experience (service as a clerk for a judge) preferred.
  6. Experience teaching law courses or legal writing at accredited law schools is a plus.
  7. Editorial experience with legal journals during law school is highly valued.

Compensation is output-based; experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required to complete work may vary depending on the expert’s experience and workflow. Minimum submission requirements apply. Experts must submit a minimum of tasks per week.


Start Timeline & Availability

We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts ready to jump in right away. If selected, we expect you to start your first tasks within 24 – 48 hours of completing onboarding.

Role Title: Gmail & Google Calendar AI Assistant Evaluator


Role Type: Contractor, Remote


Location: United States only


micro1 is engaging Gmail & Google Calendar AI Assistant Evaluators to collaborate on a customer-driven project enhancing AI assistant quality through real-world task evaluation. In this role, you'll use your everyday experience managing your digital life — email, calendars, bookings, and coordination — to help train and evaluate next-generation AI assistants. Your work will shape how AI models handle the real tasks people delegate every day.


Key Responsibilities:


  1. Complete realistic, everyday digital tasks (emailing, scheduling, booking, coordinating) using AI assistant tools under standardized, repeatable conditions.
  2. Give an AI assistant clear instructions for real-world tasks, then carefully review and verify its work for accuracy and completeness.
  3. Apply detailed grading guidelines to evaluate, rank, and annotate assistant responses, providing structured feedback that improves model performance.
  4. Test scenarios involving email threads, calendar invites, online bookings, and multi-person coordination, ensuring coverage of diverse situations and edge cases.
  5. Utilize AI training tools and platforms to record findings and submit evaluation data in alignment with project standards and milestones.
  6. Collaborate with project trainers and contributors to resolve ambiguities, refine guidelines, and ensure evaluation consistency across the team.
  7. Participate in ongoing quality reviews, incorporating feedback to maintain rigorous evaluation standards.


Required Skills and Qualifications:

  1. Are based in the US, have an iPhone with iMessage, and have a Facebook or Instagram account.
  2. Daily, hands-on use of Gmail and Google Calendar to run your own life: sending emails, accepting invites, scheduling, and rearranging plans.
  3. Regular experience coordinating with others over email or text — setting up meetups, following up on threads, or confirming shared plans and payments.
  4. Comfort booking things online independently, such as restaurants, appointments, travel, or deliveries.
  5. Experience using AI tools for real, practical tasks, with comfort giving an AI assistant instructions and checking its work.
  6. Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy when reviewing AI-generated output.
  7. Strong written communication skills for clear reporting and timely updates on progress and challenges.
  8. Demonstrated time management and self-organization for independent, remote project participation.


Preferred Qualifications:

  1. Prior experience with AI evaluation, data labeling, user testing, or similar feedback-driven projects.
  2. Familiarity with prompt writing and a practical understanding of AI assistant behaviors and limitations.
  3. Experience grading or reviewing AI outputs for accuracy, helpfulness, and safety.

Role Title: Physics Expert PhD (Statistical Physics / Quantum Information / Condensed Matter)


Role Type: Part-Time, Contractor

Location: Fully Remote, Open to candidates worlwide

Schedule: 5-10+ hrs/week. Fully flexible (Can accomodate after hours + weekends if needed)


micro1 is engaging Physics Experts (Statistical Physics / Quantum Information / Condensed Matter) to contribute to a research-driven customer project at the intersection of theoretical physics and numerical benchmarking.


In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.


Scope of Work

  1. Analyze and provide expert insights into complex statistical physics phenomena, with a focus on replicated random-bond Ising/Ashkin-Teller models, the toric-code threshold, and the Nishimori line.
  2. Deliver clear, well-documented solutions or critiques of problems relating to Kramers-Wannier duality, quenched disorder averaging, square-lattice self-duality, and domain-wall free energy.
  3. Engage in advanced numerical work, particularly around 4-state Potts model simulations and interpretation.
  4. Identify, discuss, and resolve technical challenges involving noncontractible loop defects and related topological features.
  5. Participate as a Solver, Auditor, or Adjudicator on specific project assignments based on your experience and subfield strengths.



Preferred Qualifications

  1. Advanced academic background (PhD or equivalent experience) in physics, with specialization in statistical physics, quantum information, or condensed matter theory.
  2. Direct, hands-on experience applying Kramers-Wannier duality, quenched disorder averaging, and square-lattice self-duality in research or project settings.
  3. Demonstrated proficiency in numerical simulations involving the 4-state Potts model and analysis of domain-wall free energy.
  4. Familiarity with topological quantum codes, particularly the toric code and its threshold phenomena.

Role Title: Graphic and Editorial Design Expert

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $55 to $100 per hour

Location: Fully remote, worldwide

You’ll need: Professional experience designing for print, web or publications for a company, studio, publisher or client

Your tasks: Review designs and briefs, judge layout, readability and brief match, and explain your decisions in writing


You’ll review graphic and editorial design work and judge it: what works, what doesn’t, and why. This is a good fit if you work as a graphic designer, editorial designer, layout designer or art director and make decisions about how a page, a publication or a brand piece looks and reads.


Scope of Work

  1. Look at designs (posters, covers, page layouts, brand pieces) and judge which one is stronger for a given brief and audience.
  2. Check hierarchy, spacing, type choices, color and how text and images work together.
  3. Flag problems that would show up in production (wrong format, low resolution, margins, print color).
  4. Check that a design fits the brief and the brand or publication style.
  5. Write a short explanation for each decision so a reviewer can follow your reasoning.


What we’re looking for

  1. Professional work as a graphic designer, editorial designer, layout designer, publication designer, art director or brand designer.
  2. Daily use of professional tools such as InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop or Figma.
  3. Experience with real jobs: briefs, revisions, production files and delivery to a client or publisher.
  4. Comfort explaining why one design works and another doesn’t.
  5. Clear written English.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply with your resume and a short profile.
  2. Complete the curation interview. It is a short conversation about your experience with exhibitions, collections and attribution. You don’t need to prepare, look at anything or write anything. Finishing it is what moves your application forward.
  3. Review. We check your experience against what the project needs.
  4. Onboarding and first task. If selected, you get the guidelines and start with an initial task, which is reviewed before you continue.

Role Title: Semiconductor Engineering Expert


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $80- $185/hour

Commitment: Flexible — fits alongside your current role

Location: Fully remote

You’ll need: Master’s or PhD in electrical engineering, materials, physics, or a closely related field, plus principal-level industry experience or a faculty appointment

Your tasks: Build challenging technical problems from your own domain and define what makes an answer correct


You'll be working on

The problems where the textbook answer isn’t enough, where the right approach depends on reading the constraints correctly, where a plausible-looking solution is quietly wrong. You’ll build those problems, provide the correct analysis, and define what separates a right answer from one that only looks righ


What you’ll do

  1. Design difficult technical problems from your own area — device physics, process integration, circuit design, lithography, packaging, yield and reliability — with realistic constraints and supporting data.
  2. Provide the correct solution and walk through the reasoning that gets there.
  3. Define objective criteria for correctness, so another expert reviewing the work would reach the same verdict.
  4. Review problems built by other contributors for technical accuracy and soundness of method.
  5. Flag problems that turn out to be ambiguous or ungradable rather than submitting them.


What we’re looking for

  1. Master’s or PhD in electrical engineering, materials science, applied physics, or a closely related field.
  2. Principal, staff, or fellow-level experience at a major semiconductor company, or a faculty appointment at a leading university.
  3. Deep technical depth in at least one semiconductor subdomain, with hands-on ownership of the work.
  4. Able to explain why an answer is correct clearly enough that another engineer could verify it.
  5. Publications, patents, or a record of technical leadership is a strong plus.
  6. AI or LLM evaluation experience is a plus, but not required.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview for this role — it’s how your expertise gets in front of the client
  3. Profile review
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

Role Title: Civilian Intelligence Agency Expert – U.S. & Allied Government

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote


micro1 is seeking current and former civilian professionals from U.S. and allied government intelligence agencies to contribute their specialized expertise to a project with a frontier AI lab. This opportunity is designed for individuals with firsthand experience working within intelligence organizations, including professionals from intelligence operations, technology, strategy, policy, program management, and senior leadership functions.


You will apply your knowledge of how intelligence agencies operate, make decisions, manage programs, and support national security missions to help train and evaluate next-generation AI systems.


Scope of Work


  1. Evaluate AI-generated content and scenarios involving intelligence agencies, organizational structures, operational processes, technology, and national security decision-making.
  2. Assess the accuracy, realism, and practical relevance of AI-generated responses based on your firsthand professional experience.
  3. Provide structured feedback on how intelligence organizations operate, including their responsibilities, internal workflows, coordination processes, and decision-making frameworks.
  4. Identify inaccuracies, unrealistic assumptions, or gaps in AI-generated materials and recommend improvements.
  5. Contribute to the development and review of realistic, unclassified scenarios reflecting challenges encountered by civilian intelligence professionals.
  6. Apply your expertise to improve AI systems' understanding of intelligence agency functions, professional responsibilities, and government operating environments.
  7. Communicate clear, evidence-based assessments and recommendations through written feedback.


Preferred Qualifications


  1. Direct professional experience as a civilian employee within a U.S. or allied government intelligence agency, such as the CIA, DIA, NSA, NGA, ODNI, NRO, MI5, MI6, GCHQ, or an equivalent allied intelligence organization.
  2. Experience in one or more intelligence agency functions, including:
  3. Intelligence operations, analysis, collection, or mission support.
  4. Technology, IT systems, engineering, cybersecurity, or digital transformation.
  5. Program management, organizational operations, or administrative leadership.
  6. Intelligence policy, strategic planning, governance, or interagency coordination.
  7. Senior management, executive leadership, or organizational decision-making.
  8. Strong understanding of the organizational structures, professional practices, and operating environments of civilian intelligence agencies.
  9. Ability to evaluate complex scenarios, identify inaccuracies, and provide clear, well-reasoned feedback.
  10. Excellent written English communication skills.


Learn More About Our Government & Defense Work


At micro1, we work with government and defense experts to evaluate how advanced AI models perform on real-world tasks.

Our MissionReport benchmark assesses AI-generated military and government reports, highlighting the importance of expert judgment, accuracy, and operational understanding.


Learn more: https://www.micro1.ai/benchmark/mission-report

Role Title: Manufacturing & Industrial Engineering Expert


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $80- $185/hour

Commitment: Flexible — fits alongside your current role

Location: Fully remote

You’ll need: Master’s or PhD in manufacturing, industrial, or mechanical engineering, plus principal-level industry experience or a faculty appointment

Your tasks: Build challenging technical problems from your own domain and define what makes an answer correct


You'll be working on

The problems where the textbook answer isn’t enough, where the right approach depends on reading the constraints correctly, where a plausible-looking solution is quietly wrong. You’ll build those problems, provide the correct analysis, and define what separates a right answer from one that only looks right.


What you’ll do

  1. Design difficult technical problems from your own area — process design, production systems, quality engineering, automation, supply chain and operations modeling — with realistic constraints and supporting data.
  2. Provide the correct solution and walk through the reasoning that gets there.
  3. Define objective criteria for correctness, so another expert reviewing the work would reach the same verdict.
  4. Review problems built by other contributors for technical accuracy and soundness of method.
  5. Flag problems that turn out to be ambiguous or ungradable rather than submitting them.


What we’re looking for

  1. Master’s or PhD in manufacturing, industrial, mechanical engineering, or a closely related field.
  2. Principal, staff, or fellow-level experience at a major manufacturing organization, or a faculty appointment at a leading university.
  3. Deep technical depth in at least one subdomain, with hands-on ownership of the work.
  4. Able to explain why an answer is correct clearly enough that another engineer could verify it.
  5. Publications, patents, or a record of technical leadership is a strong plus.
  6. AI or LLM evaluation experience is a plus, but not required.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview for this role — it’s how your expertise gets in front of the client
  3. Profile review
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

Role Title: Art and Photography Curators

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $55 to $100 per hour

Location: Fully remote, worldwide

You’ll need: Professional experience curating, acquiring, cataloguing or attributing art or photography for a museum, gallery, auction house, archive or collection

Your tasks: Review works and image sets, judge attribution, context and presentation, and explain your decisions in writing


You’ll review artworks and photographs and judge them: what they are, where they come from, how they should be shown and described. This is a good fit if you work as a curator, collections specialist, gallery or auction specialist, or photo archivist and make decisions about what to acquire, show or attribute.


Scope of Work

  1. Look at works or sets of works and decide which fit a given theme, show or collection.
  2. Judge attribution, date, medium, edition and print type (for example, vintage vs. later print) from what is shown and described.
  3. Flag provenance gaps, doubtful attributions and condition or display risks.
  4. Check that titles, labels and descriptions are accurate and fair to the work.
  5. Flag rights, consent or ownership issues.
  6. Write a short explanation for each decision so a reviewer can follow your reasoning.


What we’re looking for

  1. Professional work as a curator, assistant curator, collections or exhibitions specialist, gallery director, auction house specialist, art or photo archivist, or registrar.
  2. Experience with real decisions: selecting works, attributing them, planning displays or handling loans and acquisitions.
  3. For photography: familiarity with prints, editions and photographic processes.
  4. Comfort explaining why a work belongs in a show or why an attribution is doubtful.
  5. Clear written English.



How the selection process works

  1. Apply with your resume and a short profile.
  2. Complete the curation interview. It is a short conversation about your experience with exhibitions, collections and attribution. You don’t need to prepare, look at anything or write anything. Finishing it is what moves your application forward.
  3. Review. We check your experience against what the project needs.
  4. Onboarding and first task. If selected, you get the guidelines and start with an initial task, which is reviewed before you continue.

Job Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Job Summary: We are seeking seasoned transactional attorneys for a part-time role at the forefront of legal AI. This opportunity is for elite lawyers who want to help shape how advanced AI is trained, evaluated, and applied in real-world legal work, especially those who have deep experience with drafting, reviewing, negotiating, and redlining within the tech field.

  1. Perform simulated contract negotiations and redlining exercises.
  2. Review and assess AI responses to contract scenarios, providing expert feedback to improve model performance and output precision.

  4. Demonstrated commitment to innovation at the intersection of law and technology.
  5. Experience working with cross-disciplinary teams in fast-paced environments.


Preferred Qualifications:

  1. Prior exposure to AI, legal tech, or training initiatives.

Compensation Structure:


Compensation is task-based, meaning experts are paid per completed task that meets the project specifications. The average handling time (AHT) is approximately 3.5 hours per task, and the effective hourly rate will depend on the number of tasks completed and successfully signed off.
