Role Title: Art Buying and Photography Representation Expert

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $55 to $100 per hour

Location: Fully remote, worldwide

You’ll need: Professional experience commissioning, licensing or representing photographers or other visual artists for agencies, brands, publications or studios.

Your tasks: Review briefs, cost estimates and licensing cases, judge fit, price and usage terms, and explain your decisions in writing.


You’ll review briefs, estimates and image licensing situations and judge them: what makes sense, what is missing, and why. This is a good fit if you work as an art buyer, photo buyer, creative producer, photography agent or artist representative and make decisions about who gets hired, at what price and under what usage terms. You need professional experience commissioning or representing photographers or other visual artists, and clear written English.


Scope of Work

  1. Look at a brief and decide which type of photographer or artist is the best fit.
  2. Check cost estimates and flag items that are missing, padded or out of range.
  3. Judge whether usage rights (media, territory, time, exclusivity) match what the client needs and what was paid.
  4. Flag contract, release, insurance or logistics gaps that would cause problems later.
  5. Write a short explanation for each decision so a reviewer can follow your reasoning.


What we’re looking for

  1. Professional work as an art buyer, photo buyer, creative producer, agency producer, photography agent, artist representative or licensing manager.
  2. Experience with real jobs: briefs, estimates, negotiation, contracts and delivery.
  3. Working knowledge of image licensing and usage terms.
  4. Comfort explaining why one choice or one price makes sense and another doesn’t.
  5. Clear written English.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply with your resume and a short profile.
  2. Complete the curation interview. It is a short conversation about your experience with exhibitions, collections and attribution. You don’t need to prepare, look at anything or write anything. Finishing it is what moves your application forward.
  3. Review. We check your experience against what the project needs.
  4. Onboarding and first task. If selected, you get the guidelines and start with an initial task, which is reviewed before you continue.

Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote (US or India)


micro1 is engaging Tax Practitioners, Federal Individual Income Tax (CPA/EA/Tax Attorney)s to participate in a project supporting a customer. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.


Scope of Work

  1. Read and interpret federal individual income tax law, including the Internal Revenue Code, Treasury regulations, and IRS guidance at the level of specific subsections and provisions.
  2. Develop precise rubrics and checklists that define the requirements a correct answer must satisfy, grounded strictly in authoritative sources.
  3. Assign technical severity to each requirement, accurately distinguishing between critical, secondary, and minor elements.
  4. Review and evaluate AI-generated tax analyses and computations, scoring each response against your criteria for accuracy and completeness.
  5. Compose detailed, self-contained test scenarios (including edge cases) for criteria that fail, specifying facts, dates, filing status, and expected results.
  6. Identify and flag ambiguities, statutory exceptions, or conflicts in the law or guidance, providing structured written feedback within the digital review platform.
  7. Submit clear, structured written evaluations to support ongoing system improvement.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Active CPA license, Enrolled Agent designation, or experience as a US tax attorney with federal individual income tax focus.
  2. Extensive hands-on experience preparing or planning federal personal income tax matters for individuals.
  3. Demonstrated ability to read, analyze, and interpret the Internal Revenue Code, regulations, and related guidance beyond simple return preparation.
  4. Proficiency with legal logic constructs, such as conditions, thresholds, phase-outs, exceptions, and defined terms.
  5. Exceptional written communication skills with an emphasis on clarity, objectivity, and reproducibility of criteria and outcomes.
  6. Familiarity with complex return issues such as investments, self-employment income, equity compensation, rental property, or multi-state/international items.

Role Title: Imagery Analyst (Drone & Maritime)

Role Type: Contractor - part-time or full-time



Opportunity Snapshot

Compensation: $35 - $80 hourly

Volume: Steady throughput expected; you set your own pace

Commitment: Part-time or full-time, your schedule

Location: Remote (U.S.)

Eligibility: This role supports a U.S. Navy project. Under the terms of that federal contract, it requires U.S. citizenship and an active DoD Common Access Card (CAC). Applicants who don’t meet these contract requirements aren’t eligible for this project — but we run other annotation projects without them, so we’d still like to hear from you.

Your tasks: Review and correct object labels on drone and maritime imagery


micro1 is engaging imagery annotators for a Navy project working with drone and maritime sensor imagery. This role requires an active DoD Common Access Card — if you don’t have one, this project isn’t a fit, but we run other annotation projects without that requirement.


The work is precise and repetitive: you review object labels that a machine generated, fix the ones that are wrong, and add the ones it missed. No AI experience required. What matters is a careful eye and the discipline to stay accurate across long sessions.


What you’ll do

  1. Review machine-generated bounding boxes on still imagery and correct the ones that are off.
  2. Find and label objects the model missed.
  3. Apply the labeling guidelines consistently across every image.
  4. Work within a secure Navy environment using the provided tools.
  5. Maintain steady throughput — you’re paid per submitted image.
  6. Flag ambiguous cases to the team instead of guessing.
  7. Move into video frame annotation as the project expands.


What we’re looking for

  1. Active DoD Common Access Card (CAC) and U.S. citizenship, both required under the terms of this federal contract.
  2. Strong attention to detail and the patience for repetitive, accuracy-critical work.
  3. Experience with data labeling or bounding box annotation is a plus, but not required.
  4. Familiarity with aerial, maritime, satellite, or thermal imagery is a plus.
  5. Comfortable learning new labeling software.
  6. Clear written and verbal communication.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview for this role
  3. Profile review
  4. Onboarding, our Talent Ops team will get you set up

Role Title: Senior Cargo Condition and Securing Surveyor


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Global-Remote

Job Type: Contractor (~10 hours per week)

Schedule: Flexible-you choose the hours and days you work, including weekends if desired


micro1 is engaging Senior Cargo Condition and Securing Surveyors to contribute expert analysis and insight to a customer's logistics-focused project. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.


Scope of Work

  1. Evaluate refrigerated and temperature-controlled cargo documentation, such as reefer temperature logs and condition records, to assess compliance and identify potential issues.
  2. Analyze finished-vehicle and food transport evidence, including damage reports and compliance documents, to determine condition, causation, and potential losses.
  3. Perform remote assessments of container integrity, cargo securing methods, and lashing arrangements using photographic and written shipment records.
  4. Review hatch-cover inspection reports and related marine cargo documentation to assess sealing, weatherproofing, and compliance with safety standards.
  5. Write clear, professional surveyor findings and damage attributions, providing detailed reasoning for each conclusion as would be required in a signed surveyor's report.
  6. Deliver structured, written feedback to support the training and evaluation of advanced AI models focused on cargo logistics and compliance.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. At least 7 years of experience as a cargo surveyor specializing in reefer and temperature-controlled shipments, containerized cargo, or cargo securing and lashing practices.
  2. Demonstrated expertise in reviewing and interpreting photos, inspection logs, damage reports, and compliance documentation for marine or land-based logistics.
  3. Background in one or more of the following: reefer and perishables surveying, container and securing surveying, marine hatch-cover inspection, finished-vehicle logistics inspection, or food transport auditing.
  4. Strong analytical judgment and a meticulous approach to documentation review and report writing.
  5. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to provide clear, well-reasoned explanations for technical findings.
  6. Familiarity with international transportation compliance standards and best practices for cargo condition and securing.
  7. Previous consulting or remote project participation experience is a plus, though not required.

Role Title: Set and Production Design Expert

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $55 to $100 per hour

Location: Fully remote, worldwide

You’ll need: Professional experience designing, building or decorating sets for film, TV, theatre, events, commercials or photography

Your tasks: Review set designs and briefs, judge how well they fit the story, the space and the camera, and explain your decisions in writing


You’ll review set and production design work and judge it: what works, what doesn’t, and why. This is a good fit if you work as a production designer, set designer, art director or set decorator and make decisions about how a space looks and works for film, TV, theatre, events or photography. You need professional experience designing or building sets for real productions, and clear written English.


Scope of Work

  1. Look at set designs, room setups or production concepts and judge which one is stronger for a given script, brief or budget.
  2. Check scale, layout, sightlines, color, materials and how the space would work for actors and camera.
  3. Flag problems that would show up on the day (a set that does not fit the shot, a material that looks fake on camera, items wrong for the period).
  4. Check that a design fits the story, the setting and the budget.
  5. Write a short explanation for each decision so a reviewer can follow your reasoning.


What we’re looking for

  1. Professional work as a production designer, set designer, art director, set decorator, assistant art director or theatre designer.
  2. Experience with real productions: scripts or briefs, budgets, builds, shoot or install days and working with other departments.
  3. Comfort with design tools such as SketchUp, AutoCAD, Vectorworks, Rhino or Photoshop, or strong hand drafting. Not all are required.
  4. Comfort explaining why one design works and another doesn’t.
  5. Clear written English.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply with your resume and a short profile.
  2. Complete the curation interview. It is a short conversation about your experience with exhibitions, collections and attribution. You don’t need to prepare, look at anything or write anything. Finishing it is what moves your application forward.
  3. Review. We check your experience against what the project needs.
  4. Onboarding and first task. If selected, you get the guidelines and start with an initial task, which is reviewed before you continue.

Role Title: Wearable Electronic User


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is engaging Wearable Electronic Users to contribute health and activity data for a customer’s project that helps train next-generation AI systems. This is a one-time task, not an ongoing role. You export your data once, upload it once, and get paid once per device. No prior AI experience is required.


How it works

  1. Export your historical data from your wearable device account.
  2. Upload it as a ZIP file through a Google Form.
  3. Once your data passes a quality check, you’re paid $70 for that device. That’s it.


Have more than one device? Each qualifying device or account can be submitted once, and each is paid separately. For example, an Oura ring plus a Garmin watch means two submissions and $140 total.

  4. Make sure the data is in English, switching your device or app language before exporting if needed
  5. Give accurate information about your device type and how long you’ve tracked continuously


Requirements

  1. Currently use one of these devices: Oura, WHOOP, Garmin, Samsung Galaxy Watch/Samsung Health, Fitbit/Pixel Watch, or Apple Watch
  2. At least 18 months of continuous data, with no gap longer than 6 weeks
  3. Data recorded within the last 6 months
  4. Tracking of at least two of sleep, activity, or heart rate
  5. Login access to your own device account
  6. Comfortable exporting data and uploading a ZIP file through an online form
  7. Able to provide your data in English

Role Title: Aerospace Engineering Expert


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $80- $185/hour

Commitment: Flexible — fits alongside your current role

Location: Fully remote

You’ll need: Master’s or PhD in aerospace or a closely related field, plus principal-level industry experience or a faculty appointment

Your tasks: Build challenging technical problems from your own domain and define what makes an answer correct


You'll be working on

The work draws on what you already know: the problems where the textbook answer isn’t enough, where the right approach depends on reading the constraints correctly, where a plausible-looking solution is quietly wrong. You’ll build those problems, provide the correct analysis, and define what separates a right answer from one that only looks right.


What you’ll do

  1. Design difficult technical problems from your own area — aerodynamics, propulsion, structures, GNC, orbital mechanics, systems engineering — with realistic constraints and supporting data.
  2. Provide the correct solution and walk through the reasoning that gets there.
  3. Define objective criteria for correctness, so another expert reviewing the work would reach the same verdict.
  4. Review problems built by other contributors for technical accuracy and soundness of method.
  5. Flag problems that turn out to be ambiguous or ungradable rather than submitting them.


What we’re looking for

  1. Master’s or PhD in aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, or a closely related field.
  2. Principal, staff, or fellow-level experience at a major aerospace organization, or a faculty appointment at a leading university.
  3. Deep technical depth in at least one aerospace subdomain, with hands-on ownership of the work.
  4. Able to explain why an answer is correct clearly enough that another engineer could verify it.
  5. Publications, patents, or a record of technical leadership is a strong plus.
  6. AI or LLM evaluation experience is a plus, but not required.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview for this role — it’s how your expertise gets in front of the client

Role Title: VA Eligibility Specialist


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote

micro1 is looking for VA Eligibility Specialists to help evaluate and improve AI systems on veterans health care topics. Role Title: Coding Author


Role Type: Contractor


Location: US - Remote


micro1 is engaging Coding Authors (CCS / CIC / CPC certified) to contribute their expertise to a dynamic project for a valued customer. In this role, you’ll apply your coding expertise to create the training material that helps next-generation AI systems learn, reason, and perform. Your work will shape how models understand real-world medical coding. No prior experience in AI is required, your domain knowledge is what matters.


Scope of Work

  1. Author realistic medical coding scenarios, clinical documentation excerpts, and coding questions across inpatient, outpatient, and professional fee settings, with accurate ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS, CPT, and HCPCS code assignment.
  2. Write detailed answer keys and rationales that explain code selection, sequencing, modifiers, and Present on Admission (POA) indicators, citing the relevant official guidelines and coding conventions.
  3. Build evaluation rubrics and test cases of varying difficulty, including complex and ambiguous documentation, to assess how well AI models apply coding rules.
  4. Review and revise existing coding content for accuracy, clarity, and alignment with current ICD-10-CM/PCS Official Guidelines, AHA Coding Clinic, and CPT guidance.
  5. Collaborate with project stakeholders using both written and verbal communication to clarify requirements, resolve documentation ambiguities, and ensure data integrity.
  6. Deliver high-quality feedback on coding guidelines and complex cases to support project workflow improvements and enhance AI model understanding.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Active AHIMA Certified Coding Specialist (CCS), AAPC Certified Inpatient Coder (CIC), or AAPC Certified Professional Coder (CPC) credential.
  2. Thorough expertise in ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS, and CPT, with hands-on coding experience in a hospital, physician practice, or coding audit setting.
  3. Experience writing or reviewing coding content, such as training materials, audit findings, coder education, or exam preparation.
  4. Ability to explain complex coding decisions clearly and concisely in writing.
  5. Strong written and verbal communication skills, demonstrating meticulous attention to detail and clarity.
  6. Access to current ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS, and CPT code sets and Official Coding Guidelines.

Role Title: Fashion and Interior Styling Expert

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $55 to $100 per hour

Location: Fully remote, worldwide

You’ll need: Professional experience styling looks or spaces for editorial, brands, retail, productions or private clients

Your tasks: Review looks, rooms and briefs, judge fit, color, proportion and brief match, and explain your decisions in writing


You’ll review styling work for fashion and interiors and judge it: what works, what doesn’t, and why. This is a good fit if you work as a fashion stylist, wardrobe stylist, interior stylist, set stylist or home stylist and make decisions about what goes into a look or a space.


Scope of Work

  1. Look at outfits or room setups and judge which one is stronger for a given brief, season or client.
  2. Check proportion, fit, scale, color and material choices.
  3. Flag items that would not work in practice (wrong size, wrong fabric for the use, items that don’t fit the space).
  4. Judge if a look or a space fits the brief, budget and setting.
  5. Write a short explanation for each decision so a reviewer can follow your reasoning.
  6. Write or improve styling briefs, mood descriptions or shopping lists.


What we’re looking for

  1. Professional work as a fashion stylist, wardrobe stylist, personal stylist, interior stylist, set stylist, prop stylist or home stylist.
  2. Experience with real jobs: briefs, sourcing, fittings or installs, and delivery to a client.
  3. Comfort explaining why one look or space works and another doesn’t.
  4. Clear written English


How the selection process works

  1. Apply with your resume and a short profile.
  2. Complete the curation interview. It is a short conversation about your experience with exhibitions, collections and attribution. You don’t need to prepare, look at anything or write anything. Finishing it is what moves your application forward.
  3. Review. We check your experience against what the project needs.
  4. Onboarding and first task. If selected, you get the guidelines and start with an initial task, which is reviewed before you continue.

About the opportunity

micro1 is looking for experienced Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) professionals with expertise in SysML v1 and exposure to SysML v2, or hands-on experience with SysML v2 textual modeling, to support a customer project focused on AI training and evaluation.

In this role, you’ll apply your systems engineering knowledge to develop reference models, assess AI-generated SysML v2 outputs, and establish clear standards for technical accuracy and model quality.

Your expertise will help evaluate how effectively AI systems interpret engineering requirements, represent complex system architectures, and produce consistent, traceable models.

  4. Review, assess, and provide structured feedback on SysML v2 models, ensuring technical accuracy and adherence to modeling best practices.
  5. Analyze requirements, Concepts of Operations (ConOps), Interface Control Documents (ICDs), and architectural specifications to inform modeling efforts.

Role Title: Humanitarian Aid Representative


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is engaging Humanitarian Aid Representatives to contribute their field expertise in humanitarian and civilian protection for a unique project. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters. The focus of this engagement is to design, review, and refine scenarios involving civilian harm, protected persons, and the boundaries of legitimate activity, ensuring responses are grounded in International Humanitarian Law (IHL) and best practices in humanitarian action. Strong written and verbal communication skills are highly valued, as your insights and documentation will directly influence AI performance and sensitivity to complex humanitarian concerns.


Scope of Work

  1. Develop nuanced cases and scenarios focused on civilian protection, proportionality, and humanitarian constraints for AI model evaluation.
  2. Assess and grade AI-generated responses for accuracy, depth of reasoning, and sensitivity to civilian-harm considerations.
  3. Identify and flag instances of excessive caution or insufficient restraint in model responses, highlighting humanitarian implications.
  4. Document challenging or ambiguous cases from a humanitarian perspective to inform future training and refinement.
  5. Collaborate with project stakeholders to clarify humanitarian concepts and contribute to guidance on IHL-related reasoning.
  6. Maintain precise, clear, and context-rich records of findings and recommendations.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Background in humanitarian operations, protection, or policy with organizations such as ICRC/Red Cross, UN agencies, or major NGOs.
  2. Strong grounding in International Humanitarian Law and civilian-protection principles.
  3. Experience in teaching, training, or field leadership related to humanitarian action or IHL dissemination.
  4. Exceptional written and verbal English communication skills, especially in crafting and reviewing complex case material.
  5. Proven ability to apply proportionality reasoning in conflict or protection scenarios.
  6. Experience documenting or reporting on edge cases or challenging humanitarian situations.
  7. Conflict-zone fieldwork, protection-cluster participation, or IHL-dissemination experience is highly valued.

At micro1, we work with government and defense experts to evaluate how advanced AI models perform on real-world tasks.

Our MissionReport benchmark assesses AI-generated military and government reports, highlighting the importance of expert judgment, accuracy, and operational understanding.

In this role, you'll evaluate inpatient clinical documentation (H&Ps, progress notes, discharge summaries) for clinical accuracy, completeness, and fidelity to the patient encounter. Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote

Role Title: Paid Photo Contributor Opportunity (Siblings)

Location: Remote


Job Summary

micro1 is recruiting sibling pairs or groups to participate in a paid photo data collection project supporting the development and evaluation of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.


What you'll do:

  1. Each sibling takes and submits 30 selfies and 60 videos of themselves (individually and/or together) following simple project instructions.
  2. Each sibling completes a short questionnaire about themselves and the submitted images.
  3. Complete the project remotely using your own smartphones.


Who we're looking for:

The project is designed to create a dataset representing people from a broad range of racial and ethnic backgrounds and physical appearances, including data that helps AI systems better understand visual similarity between family members. We are seeking participation from siblings (2 or more) across many different communities and backgrounds.


Religious and cultural attire:

Participants are welcome to wear religious or cultural attire and accessories in their photos, including but not limited to hijabs, turbans, kippahs, and religious jewelry. These are fully accepted, and there is no need to remove them. We want the dataset to reflect how people actually present themselves.


Sibling groups of all racial and ethnic backgrounds are welcome to apply.


Compensation: u$140 per approved task, per participant

Eligibility: 18+ / NAMER, LATAM, EMEA / smartphone / must have at least one sibling willing to also participate

Role Title: Materials Scientist (Nanoparticle Sizing & Lot Release)


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is engaging Materials Scientists (Nanoparticle Sizing & Lot Release) to contribute specialized expertise to a customer’s project focused on advanced nanomaterial evaluation. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters. This opportunity centers on thorough nanoparticle sizing, particle size distribution analysis, and lot release qualifications using Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) and Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM). The engagement emphasizes independent expert analysis — including manual image thresholding, calibration, and morphology assessments — without reliance on automated or AI-powered tools. Strong written and verbal communication skills are essential to document findings, interpret complex micrographs, and convey critical decisions to project stakeholders.


Scope of Work


  1. Manually analyze and interpret TEM and SEM micrographs for nanoparticle sizing and morphological assessment
  2. Determine and document particle size distributions (PSD) with rigorous attention to accuracy and reproducibility
  3. Establish and communicate lot-release acceptance criteria based on technical reference cases and quality control standards
  4. Prepare detailed reports summarizing findings, methodologies, and recommendations for material qualification
  5. Validate measurement techniques through manual calibration, thresholding, and cross-checking against reference data
  6. Participate in technical discussions, providing expert insights on nanomaterial characterization and quality control criteria
  7. Deliver clear, concise written and verbal communications to facilitate knowledge transfer across project teams


Preferred Qualifications


  1. Advanced knowledge of nanomaterial characterization, especially using TEM and SEM
  2. Demonstrated hands-on experience in nanoparticle sizing, particle size distribution analysis, and lot release evaluation
  3. Proficiency with manual image analysis, including thresholding, calibration, and interpretation of complex morphologies
  4. Strong understanding of quality control standards and reference material qualification protocols
  5. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills for reporting and collaboration
  6. Ability to evaluate and validate technical reference cases without the use of AI-based tools
  7. Background in scientific consulting, materials science, or laboratory-based analytical roles is a plus

Role Title: Computational Chemistry, Structural Biology & Drug Discovery Scientist (PhD)


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote (Worldwide)


Job Summary: In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input.


Key Responsibilities

  1. Design and write challenging, expert-level scientific problems in computational chemistry, structural biology, and drug discovery, with clear, verifiable solutions.
  2. Review and evaluate AI model outputs for scientific accuracy, rigor, and depth of reasoning, identifying subtle errors that non-specialists would miss.
  3. Develop detailed rubrics and reference answers grounded in the primary literature and established methodology.
  4. Apply domain expertise across areas such as molecular modeling and simulation, protein structure prediction and design, virtual screening and docking, QSAR/ADMET modeling, and proteomics/metabolomics data analysis.
  5. Provide clear written explanations of your reasoning, so that other experts can follow and validate it.
  6. Meet quality standards through iterative feedback and peer review cycles.


Required Qualifications (MUST)

  1. PhD in Computational Chemistry, Structural Biology, Biophysics, Bioinformatics, Medicinal Chemistry, Biochemistry, or a closely related field.
  2. Hands-on research experience in an academic or industry lab (wetlab experience is a plus).
  3. Professional written and spoken English (C1 or higher).


Preferred Skills

  1. Postdoctoral or industry research experience (pharma/biotech) in drug discovery or structural biology.
  2. Strong publication record, particularly first-author papers in relevant journals.
  3. Molecular modeling and simulation: GROMACS, AMBER, NAMD, OpenMM, free energy methods (FEP/TI).
  4. Structure prediction and design: AlphaFold, Rosetta, homology modeling, cryo-EM / X-ray crystallography data interpretation.
  5. Docking and virtual screening: AutoDock, Glide, Schrödinger Suite, MOE.
  6. Cheminformatics: RDKit, QSAR/QSPR, ADMET prediction, fingerprinting, library design.
  7. Proteomics and metabolomics: LC-MS/MS, MaxQuant, DIA/DDA workflows, PTM analysis, untargeted metabolomics.
  8. Programming: Python (required in practice), plus R, Bash, or similar; experience with ML for molecular property prediction (GNNs, generative models) is a plus.
  9. Experience with benchmarking, model evaluation, or scientific writing/reviewing.
  10. Ability to explain complex scientific concepts clearly and precisely in writing.

Role Title: Smartwatch User


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Job Summary


Get paid from home in this fully remote AI research project by sharing an export of your own wearable health data. If you own and actively wear an Oura, WHOOP, Garmin, Samsung Galaxy Watch (Samsung Health), Google Fitbit/Pixel Watch, or Apple Watch for a year and a half or more, your history could help train and evaluate AI models.


You’ll download your data export from your device account and upload it as a ZIP file through a Google Form. No special equipment is needed besides the weareble tech.


Key Responsibilities

  2. Data history: At least 18 months of continuous data, with no gap longer than 6 weeks.
  3. Recent activity: Data recorded within the last 6 months.
  4. Data types: Tracking of at least two of the following: sleep, activity, or heart rate.
  5. Account access: Login access to your own device account.
  6. Technical comfort: Able to download files and upload a ZIP through a Google Form.
  7. Able to follow instructions, pay attention to detail, and work independently.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Data from multiple devices or accounts.
  2. 3+ years of history.
  3. Broad data coverage across multiple categories, such as sleep, fitness, activity, and heart rate.


Compensation Structure:

  1. You will receive a payment of $70 per data of device submitted, paid after your data is reviewed and meets the project requirements.

Role Title: Federal Civil Litigation Attorney


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is engaging experienced Federal Civil Litigation Attorneys to contribute their legal expertise to a cutting-edge AI research initiative. In this role, you'll help improve how next-generation AI systems draft, evaluate, and refine legal arguments and court motions. We're looking for practicing attorneys with strong federal civil litigation experience and a proven track record of successful motion practice. You'll use your professional judgment to assess the quality, persuasiveness, and structure of AI-generated legal writing, providing feedback that reflects real-world litigation standards.


Scope of Work


  1. Review and compare AI-generated legal motions, assessing their persuasiveness, structure, clarity, tone, and overall quality.
  2. Rank different versions of legal motions and provide clear explanations of your preferences and reasoning.
  3. Evaluate whether AI-generated motions meet professional standards and identify areas requiring improvement.
  4. Edit and refine legal motions to a ready-to-file standard, providing feedback on the changes made.
  5. Develop realistic motion-writing assignments based on federal civil litigation scenarios.
  6. Create evaluation criteria to assess the quality and effectiveness of AI-generated legal arguments.
  7. Apply practical litigation experience to identify what makes legal writing persuasive, well-structured, and effective in court.


Preferred Qualifications


  1. Juris Doctor (JD) degree and active U.S. bar membership in good standing.
  2. Practicing attorney with substantial hands-on experience in federal civil litigation and motion drafting.
  3. A proven track record of winning at least three court motions, with the ability to provide supporting court filings during the screening process.
  4. Strong experience drafting substantive motions, including motions to dismiss, motions for summary judgment, or similar federal court filings.
  5. Excellent legal research, analytical, and persuasive writing skills.
  6. Ability to critically evaluate legal arguments and clearly explain what makes one approach more effective than another.
  7. Strong attention to detail, particularly in legal reasoning, citation accuracy, document structure, and professional writing standards.
  8. Experience in appellate litigation or a previous judicial clerkship combined with litigation practice is also highly relevant.

STEM Expert

Pay: $60–$120/hour

Location: Global, fully remote

Job Type: Contractor (~15 hours per week)

Schedule: Flexible—you choose the hours and days you work, including weekends if desired


We are looking for highly skilled STEM and scientific-domain experts to contribute to an AI training project involving technical problem-solving, scientific reasoning, data analysis, and Python.


The work involves solving, reviewing, and validating challenging problems within your area of expertise. A representative task may require analyzing a scientific or mathematical problem, developing a rigorous solution, using Python to perform calculations or simulations, and evaluating whether an AI-generated answer is technically correct.

This is a very coding heavy role. Candidates but have experience using coding agents in their workflow.

Candidates are not expected to be experts across every STEM discipline. We are looking for deep expertise in at least one of the following areas:

  1. Chemistry
  2. Biology
  3. Mathematics
  4. Physics
  5. Earth Science / Geoscience / Environmental Science
  6. Robotics

Adjacent scientific or quantitative disciplines may also be considered where the candidate's expertise is directly relevant.

What You’ll Work On

  1. Solve complex scientific, mathematical, or technical problems within your domain of expertise.
  2. Review AI-generated solutions for factual, mathematical, and scientific correctness.
  3. Identify incorrect assumptions, reasoning errors, missing constraints, and subtle technical mistakes.

Required Qualifications

  1. Strong expertise in at least one relevant STEM or scientific domain.
  2. Practical proficiency with Python or other coding languages.
  3. Strong scientific, mathematical, or quantitative problem-solving ability.

Relevant Python tools may include NumPy, SciPy, pandas, SymPy, Jupyter, or domain-specific scientific libraries. No particular Python library is mandatory.


Expertise may come from academic research, industry, teaching, engineering, independent technical work, or other demonstrated experience. A specific degree or number of years of experience is not strictly required if you can demonstrate strong expertise in your field.


Process

  1. Apply to the role and complete the screening questions.
  2. Complete an AI interview of approximately 30 minutes.
  3. Complete the hiring manager review.


Compensation Structure


Compensation is output-based. Experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required to complete each task may vary depending on the expert’s experience and workflow.

Minimum submission requirements apply.


Start Timeline & Availability

We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts who are ready to begin immediately. If selected, you will be expected to start your first task within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.

Role Title: HR & People Operations Expert


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote, global


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: Up to $90/hour equivalent

Time per task: ~10 hours per task

Location: Fully remote — no geographic restrictions. Strong English required (B2 minimum, C1 preferred)

Next step: Complete the role-specific AI interview — it’s how your expertise gets in front of the client

Your tasks: Design realistic, multi-step HR and people operations tasks with objective criteria for grading the output


micro1 is engaging experienced HR and people operations practitioners to design the tasks that measure what AI systems can actually do. Your domain knowledge is what matters here — no prior AI experience required.


The work is to turn real HR workflows into benchmark tasks: realistic, difficult, and gradable against objective criteria. If you’ve written a policy, built a payroll checklist, or trained someone to handle employee cases against a standard, that’s the instinct this needs.


Scope of Work

  1. Design multi-step tasks drawn from real HR work — payroll operations, workforce planning, policy application, employee lifecycle processes — with realistic reference files and clear instructions.
  2. Define objective grading criteria so two qualified reviewers would reach the same verdict on the same output.
  3. Build tasks that require judgment rather than lookup: ones where the right answer depends on reading the materials correctly.
  4. Create or source the supporting materials each task needs: policy documents, payroll reports, headcount data, employment agreements.
  5. Flag tasks that turn out to be ambiguous or ungradable instead of submitting them anyway.
  6. Deliver approved tasks on schedule and at the required quality level.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. 5+ years of hands-on responsibility in payroll, workforce planning, HR policy, or employee lifecycle operations — direct ownership of the work, not supervisory-only or adjacent exposure.
  2. Experience creating or applying structured standards: HR policies, payroll checklists, process documentation, compliance frameworks, or training assessments.
  3. Comfortable working across spreadsheets, reports, and policy documents at the same time.
  4. HR certification (SHRM, CIPD, PHR or equivalent) is a plus, but not required.
  5. Strong English, written and spoken — B2 minimum, C1 preferred.
  6. AI or LLM evaluation experience is a plus, but not required.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview for this role — even if you’ve interviewed with us before, a role-specific interview is how we showcase your domain expertise to the client, and it gives you the strongest shot at being selected
  3. Profile review
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

Role Title: English Teacher


Role Type: Contractor, Remote


Location: United States only


micro1 is engaging English Teachers to collaborate on a customer-driven project that improves AI assistant quality through real-world task evaluation. In this role, you'll draw on your academic background and classroom experience, including managing student and parent communication, schedules, and coordination, to help train and evaluate next-generation AI assistants. Your expertise in language, literature, writing, and precise instruction following will shape how AI models handle the everyday tasks people delegate.


Key Responsibilities:

  1. Complete realistic teaching-related digital tasks (emailing parents and students, scheduling conferences, booking field trips to theaters or author events, coordinating with colleagues) using AI assistant tools under standardized, repeatable conditions.
  2. Read detailed task instructions and grading guidelines closely and follow them precisely and consistently, including multi-step requirements and fine details.
  3. Give an AI assistant clear instructions for real-world tasks, then review its work for accuracy, tone, grammar, completeness, and whether it followed the instructions given.
  4. Apply detailed grading guidelines to evaluate, rank, and annotate assistant responses, with a focus on language quality, literary and stylistic appropriateness, clarity, and tone.
  5. Draw on your knowledge of literature, rhetoric, and composition to judge whether AI-written text is well-constructed, audience-appropriate, and faithful to the request.
  6. Use AI training tools and platforms to record findings and submit evaluation data in line with project standards and milestones.


Required Skills and Qualifications:

  1. Based in the US, with an iPhone with iMessage and a Facebook and/or Instagram account.
  2. Bachelor's degree in English, literature, creative writing, linguistics, comparative literature, education, or a related humanities field.
  3. Strong instruction-following skills: the ability to read detailed, multi-step guidelines carefully and apply every requirement accurately, without skipping or reinterpreting steps.
  4. Experience teaching English or literature (for example, language arts, literature, composition, creative writing, or ESL) at the K-12, college, or adult education level.
  5. Solid knowledge of literary analysis, writing conventions, and grammar, with the ability to evaluate text for style, tone, and clarity.
  6. Daily, hands-on use of Google Classroom to run your classes: posting assignments and announcements, giving feedback on student work, managing due dates, and communicating with students and parents, alongside regular use of Gmail and Google Calendar.
  7. Experience using AI tools for real, practical tasks, with comfort giving an AI assistant instructions and checking its work.
  8. Exceptional attention to detail in grammar, tone, and accuracy when reviewing AI-generated writing.


Preferred Qualifications:

  1. Master's degree or advanced coursework in English, literature, or a related field.
  2. Prior experience with AI evaluation, data labeling, user testing, or similar feedback-driven projects.
  3. Familiarity with prompt writing and a practical understanding of AI assistant behaviors and limitations.
  4. Experience grading or reviewing writing or AI outputs for accuracy, helpfulness, and appropriateness.
  5. Experience writing rubrics or giving structured feedback on student writing or literary analysis.

Role Title: AI Agent Tester — Real-World Tasks


Role Type: Contractor


Location: U.S based


Opportunity Snapshot


Pay: $25-45/hour

Time per task: ~1.5 hours per run (evidence and scoring included)

Project kickoff: Already active.

Onboarding: Within 24–48 hours of being selected, you’ll receive the offer and complete onboarding. You’ll begin tasking as soon as tasks are assigned.

You’ll need: An active personal AI assistant account (Plus tier), active Muse and Dots access, a smartphone that can screen record, and a payment card you can use for test purchases that are reimbursed afterward

Your tasks: Run everyday errands with two AI agents, approve key steps, screen record, and score the results


About the role


AI agents are starting to handle real-life errands: paying bills, booking trips, doing the groceries. We want to know how well they actually do it, from the point of view of a real user. That’s you.

You’ll test two AI agents side by side, using your own accounts on your phone, and tell us what worked, what didn’t, and how it felt.


What you’ll do

  1. Run real-life scenarios: bills, returns, email follow-ups, bookings, shopping, groceries, travel, family logistics, outings, and forms
  2. Approve or stop the agent at key steps
  3. Screen record every attempt
  4. Score each run on completion, quality, control issues, satisfaction, and time
  5. Share clear written feedback on the agent experience


Who we’re looking for

  1. US-based, with a Bachelor’s degree
  2. Someone who already uses AI in daily life
  3. 2-3 years of experience, preferably in engineering, business management, or office/operations
  4. Detail-oriented, great at following instructions and documenting each step
  5. Clear written communication
  6. Generalists welcome, domain experts preferred
  7. No coding or AI background needed


Why you’ll like it

  1. Get paid to use the AI tools you already use
  2. Work entirely from your phone, on your schedule
  3. Have a direct say in how next-generation AI agents get built and improved


How the selection process works

  1. Apply
  2. Complete the screening questions
  3. Interview: 15-30 minutes max
  4. Profile review: if everything looks good, we present you to the client
  5. Onboarding: our Talent Ops team will contact you to get you started

Role Title: Principal Research Scientist (Computer Science / Computational Physics)


Role Type: Contractor (flexible, Part-Time or Full-Time)


Location: Remote


micro1 is engaging Principal Research Scientist (Computer Science / Computational Physics)s to contribute to an advanced customer project at the intersection of computational theory and AI. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters. You will work with frontier AI models and agents to tackle open problems, drive research direction, and define standards for scientific breakthroughs. Your insights and rigorous approach will be pivotal in charting what counts as genuine progress within your subfield.


Scope of Work

  1. Identify, frame, and articulate foundational open problems, theoretical bounds, or simulation challenges where verifiable progress can be demonstrated.
  2. Guide AI models and agents in multi-step research processes—ranging from proofs and algorithms to numerical experiments and high-performance simulations.
  3. Critically assess and validate results, utilizing proof checks, computational reproduction, and formal methods to pinpoint the limits of model-generated reasoning.
  4. Evaluate and document the novelty, correctness, and significance of research outputs relative to current literature and established results.
  5. Produce clear, concise research memos detailing research attempts, partial solutions, and observed model limitations or failure patterns.
  6. Advise on research directions, recommending promising subfields and open problems suitable for advancement via AI models and computational tools.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. 7 - 10+ years of active research in computer science or mathematical/computational physics, with a strong record of scholarly contributions.
  2. Recognition at the field level—such as major prizes, society fellowships, or plenary/invited talks at top scholarly events.
  3. A consistent publication record in leading venues within your domain, with recent results published in the past year.
  4. Demonstrated success resolving named open problems or introducing influential concepts adopted by peers.
  5. Deep, hands-on experience with computational research methods: simulation, numerical analysis, algorithmic implementation, and/or high-performance computing environments.
  6. Proven ability to rigorously examine technical work outside your immediate area of expertise.
  7. Experience on program committees, editorial boards, or with formal research tools (e.g., Lean, Coq, SAT/SMT solvers) is a strong plus, as is a public record of outlining open problems or showcasing research with advanced AI systems.

Role Title: Medical Coder


Role Type: Contractor


Location: United States, Remote


micro1 is engaging Medical Coders to contribute their expertise to a dynamic project for a valued customer. In this role, you'll apply your outpatient coding expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required. Your domain knowledge is what matters.


Scope of Work

  1. Annotate and review outpatient medical records (physician office, clinic, ambulatory surgery, and hospital outpatient encounters), ensuring accurate assignment of ICD-10-CM and CPT/HCPCS codes based on documentation.
  2. Apply Evaluation & Management (E&M) leveling to outpatient visits using official guidelines (medical decision making or total time) to validate and enrich datasets.
  3. Apply outpatient-specific coding conventions, including diagnosis coding guidelines for outpatient services, modifier usage, medical necessity, and linking diagnoses to procedures.
  4. Collaborate with project stakeholders via written and verbal communication to clarify requirements and resolve ambiguities in clinical documentation.
  5. Provide high-quality feedback on coding guidelines and edge cases to improve project workflows and model understanding.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Active AAPC Certified Professional Coder (CPC) certification is required.
  2. Comprehensive understanding of ICD-10-CM and CPT coding systems and outpatient E&M leveling guidelines.
  3. Hands-on experience coding in outpatient settings (e.g., primary care, specialty clinics, ambulatory surgery centers, outpatient hospital departments).
  4. Experience with diverse clinical documentation types and associated coding challenges, such as office visit notes, procedure notes, and operative reports.
  5. Proficiency with both written and verbal communication, with a strong attention to clarity and detail.
  6. Access to up-to-date official ICD-10-CM, CPT, and HCPCS Level II coding books, as well as E&M guidelines.


Compensation Structure:


Compensation is task-based, meaning experts are paid per completed task that meets the project specifications. The average handling time (AHT) is approximately 1 hour per task, and the effective hourly rate will depend on the number of tasks completed and successfully signed off times the selected rate.

Job Type: Contractor


Location: Remote, Japan-based.


Job Summary


Help train the next generation of personal robotics. You'll capture high-quality video demonstrations of everyday household tasks using a UMI gripper, a wearable device that mimics a robot's hand while letting you perform tasks naturally. Your demonstrations become training data that teaches robots how to operate in real homes.


Key Responsibilities


  1. Capture and submit high-quality, specification-compliant video demonstrations of everyday household tasks using a UMI gripper wearable device.
  2. Follow detailed, task-specific instructions to ensure all recordings meet rigorous project standards.
  3. Review feedback from assigned reviewers and iteratively refine your approach to improve data quality.
  4. Operate and set up recording equipment and the UMI gripper to accurately mimic real-world hand movements while performing tasks.
  5. Maintain a consistent weekly workflow to meet the minimum approved data requirements.


Required Skills and Qualifications


  1. Keen attention to detail and demonstrated ability to follow complex specifications precisely.
  2. Manual dexterity and experience with physical task precision in varied household environments.
  3. Comfort with operating, wearing, and setting up specialized devices and recording equipment.
  4. Capacity to incorporate feedback and make iterative improvements to processes and outputs.
  5. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including openness to prompt feedback exchanges.
  6. Reliable access to a fully equipped Japanese household environment (kitchen, living spaces, and common items).
  7. Ability to upload large video files via stable, high-speed internet from your home environment.
  8. This role involves prolonged use of a VR headset; candidates should be comfortable with extended wear as part of their regular work environment.


Preferred Qualifications


  1. Genuine curiosity about personal robotics, AI, and emerging technology in home environments.
  2. Prior experience participating in data collection, usability studies, or similar hands-on projects.
  3. Patience for repetitive, precision-oriented work and willingness to adapt as project needs evolve.


Compensation structure

Start at a standard rate of $12/hour, with the opportunity to increase your effective hourly earnings to $21/hour as you become more efficient.

Location: US - Remote


micro1 is engaging Inpatient Coding Specialists (CCS / CIC certified) to contribute their expertise to a dynamic project for a valued customer.   1. Annotate and review inpatient medical records, including admission notes, progress notes, operative reports, consults, lab and imaging results, and discharge summaries, ensuring precise ICD-10-CM and ICD-10-PCS code assignment based on documentation.

  5. Strong written and verbal communication skills, demonstrating meticulous attention to detail and clarity.
  6. Access to current ICD-10-CM and ICD-10-PCS code sets, Official Coding Guidelines, and MS-DRG grouper tools.

  3. Experience coding in diverse inpatient settings, such as acute care, teaching hospitals, specialty units, surgical, trauma, oncology, cardiology, and transplant cases.

  5. Strong written and verbal communication skills, demonstrating meticulous attention to detail and clarity.

Role Title: Principal Engineer / Professor — Technical Expert


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $80- $185/hour

Commitment: Flexible — fits alongside your current role

Location: Fully remote

You’ll need: Master’s or PhD in an engineering or physical science field, plus principal-level industry experience or a faculty appointment

Your tasks: Build challenging technical problems from your own domain and define what makes an answer correct


micro1 is engaging principal-level engineers, scientists, and faculty to design the technical problems that measure what AI systems can actually do. Your domain expertise is what matters here — no prior AI experience required.


We’re building this across four areas: aerospace, semiconductors, manufacturing and industrial engineering, and materials science. If your work sits in one of those — or across two of them — this is for you.


The work draws on what you already know: the problems where the textbook answer isn’t enough, where the right approach depends on reading the constraints correctly, where a plausible-looking solution is quietly wrong.


What you’ll do

  1. Design difficult technical problems from your own area, with realistic constraints and supporting data.
  2. Provide the correct solution and walk through the reasoning that gets there.
  3. Define objective criteria for correctness, so another expert reviewing the work would reach the same verdict.
  4. Review problems built by other contributors for technical accuracy and soundness of method.
  5. Flag problems that turn out to be ambiguous or ungradable rather than submitting them.

What we’re looking for

  1. Master’s or PhD in engineering, physics, materials, or a closely related field.
  2. Principal, staff, or fellow-level experience at a major engineering organization, a national lab, or a faculty appointment at a leading university.
  3. Deep technical depth in at least one area, with hands-on ownership of the work.
  4. Able to explain why an answer is correct clearly enough that another expert could verify it.
  5. Publications, patents, or a record of technical leadership is a strong plus.

How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview for this role
  3. Profile review
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

Compensation is output-based. Experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required to complete each task may vary depending on the expert’s experience and workflow.

Minimum submission requirements apply.

Start Timeline & Availability

  1. We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts who are ready to begin immediately. If selected, you will be expected to start your first task within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.

Role Title: Materials Science Expert


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $80- $185/hour

Commitment: Flexible — fits alongside your current role

Location: Fully remote

You’ll need: Master’s or PhD in materials science or a closely related field, plus principal-level industry experience or a faculty appointment

Your tasks: Build challenging technical problems from your own domain and define what makes an answer correct


You'll be working on

The problems where the textbook answer isn’t enough, where the right approach depends on reading the constraints correctly, where a plausible-looking solution is quietly wrong. You’ll build those problems, provide the correct analysis, and define what separates a right answer from one that only looks right.


What you’ll do

  1. Design difficult technical problems from your own area — structure-property relationships, processing, characterization, failure analysis, computational materials — with realistic constraints and supporting data.
  2. Provide the correct solution and walk through the reasoning that gets there.
  3. Define objective criteria for correctness, so another expert reviewing the work would reach the same verdict.
  4. Review problems built by other contributors for technical accuracy and soundness of method.
  5. Flag problems that turn out to be ambiguous or ungradable rather than submitting them.


What we’re looking for

  1. Master’s or PhD in materials science, metallurgy, ceramics, polymer science, condensed matter physics, or a closely related field.
  2. Principal, staff, or fellow-level experience in industrial or national lab research, or a faculty appointment at a leading university.
  3. Deep technical depth in at least one materials subdomain, with hands-on ownership of the work.
  4. Able to explain why an answer is correct clearly enough that another scientist could verify it.
  5. Publications, patents, or a record of technical leadership is a strong plus.
  6. AI or LLM evaluation experience is a plus, but not required.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview for this role — it’s how your expertise gets in front of the client
  3. Profile review
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

Role Title: SaaS Contracts Counsel


Job Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Job Summary: We are seeking seasoned SaaS Contracts Counsels for a part-time role at the forefront of legal AI.   1. This is an opportunity to work at the intersection of law and technology.
  2. You will help define how AI is developed for a new generation of legal practitioners.
  3. You will apply your experience in a high-impact research environment.

Role Title: Financial Due Diligence & Transaction Accounting Expert

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote - US/Canada preferred; UK and Latin America also considered

Pay: $60-120/hr. Paid per task

Time commitment: 10+ hours/week required; 20+ preferred.

Time per task: Approximately 3 hours, following approximately 15 hours of initial environment development. Estimates include agent execution time.

Your tasks: Primarily review transaction-related financial analyses and AI-generated deliverables, and help develop task instructions and objective evaluation criteria.

micro1 is engaging experienced financial due diligence and transaction accounting professionals to help build tasks that measure how effectively AI systems can perform complex transaction work.

You’ll apply your transaction expertise to review realistic financial analyses, challenge assumptions, and identify material errors. Hands-on experience with agentic AI tools is required: you’ll work with agents to support analysis and independently verify the quality of their outputs.

Scope of Work

  1. Review financial due diligence, quality-of-earnings, and carve-out financial analyses for accuracy, completeness, and supporting evidence.
  2. Identify unsupported adjustments, reconciliation issues, double counting, and inconsistent accounting treatment.
  3. Use agentic AI tools to support review and help develop realistic transaction materials, task instructions, and objective grading criteria.

Required Qualifications

  1. 5+ years of professional experience, including substantive hands-on work in financial due diligence, transaction services, or carve-out financial analysis.
  2. Direct responsibility for preparing or reviewing transaction-related financial analyses and deliverables. Audit experience or a CPA alone is insufficient.
  3. Hands-on experience using agentic AI tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or Claude Cowork for substantive work. General chatbot use alone is insufficient.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Experience at a Big Four firm or another leading transaction advisory practice.
  2. CPA qualification.
  3. Experience developing review standards, training junior professionals, or writing internal playbooks.
  4. Prior benchmark development or AI evaluation experience.

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions.

Role Type: Contractor


Location: United States, Remote


micro1 is engaging with Physician AI Trainer – Hospital Medicine to contribute their medical expertise to a customer project focused on inpatient care and documentation standards.   6. Strong attention to detail and ability to follow clear guidelines consistently.
  7. Experience with chart review, clinical documentation improvement, utilization review, or medical coding/QA is a plus.


Compensation Structure

  1. Compensation is output-based; experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required to complete work may vary depending on the expert’s experience and workflow. Minimum submission requirements apply. Experts must submit a minimum of tasks per week.

Role Title: Combat Arms & Targeting SME


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is engaging Combat Arms & Targeting subject-matter experts to support a cutting-edge project for a defense-focused customer. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.


Scope of Work

  1. Map authentic military-activity scenarios to an approved taxonomy, clearly delineating between conceptual explanation, lawful policy/readiness support, evidence curation, and the controlled boundary with operational decision support, destructive execution, autonomous weapons, and unlawful planning.
  2. Identify and propose nuanced or non-obvious boundary cases that might be misclassified by less-experienced reviewers, ensuring nuanced judgment is captured.
  3. Evaluate and grade AI-generated responses for source handling, proper expression of uncertainty (such as conflicting pattern-of-life intelligence), reasoning quality, stated limitations, and operational utility.
  4. Flag instances where AI models incorrectly refuse to engage with valid conceptual or policy questions, supporting the ongoing refinement of model parameters.
  5. Document edge cases, gray areas, and points of disagreement, maintaining a defensible and transparent answer key for model training and review processes.
  6. Support continuous refinement of project guidelines by sharing insights from operational, targeting, and fires expertise.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Extensive hands-on experience in joint or service-specific fires, targeting, or weapons employment decision-making (e.g., combat pilot, battle manager, JTAC, field or air-defense artillery officer, naval strike officer, carrier air-wing targeteer, or Aegis-qualified TAO/IAMD WTI).
  2. Advanced tactical training, such as TOPGUN, USAF Weapons School, Joint Firepower Course, or non-US allied equivalents.
  3. Demonstrated teaching, leadership, or evaluative experience (e.g., WTI, instructor, mission commander, or debrief facilitator).
  4. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to articulate operational judgment clearly and succinctly.
  5. Strong capability to assess targeting and fires utility, discriminate boundaries, and provide clear justifications.
  6. Law-of-armed-conflict or rules-of-engagement fluency from an operational perspective (not a legal role), considered a plus.
  7. Experience with AI model evaluation, wargaming, or red-teaming is valued but not required.


Learn More About Our Government & Defense Work


At micro1, we work with government and defense experts to evaluate how advanced AI models perform on real-world tasks.

Our MissionReport benchmark assesses AI-generated military and government reports, highlighting the importance of expert judgment, accuracy, and operational understanding.

Role Title: Senior Protection Engineer (Medium Voltage / Utility Distribution)


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is engaging Senior Protection Engineer (Medium Voltage / Utility Distribution) experts to contribute their technical expertise to a customer's project in the utility distribution sector. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.


Scope of Work

  1. Assess and validate protection system reference cases, including relay settings, coordination curves, and protection logs for medium voltage utility distribution networks.
  2. Review and provide feedback on technical documentation related to protective relaying and device coordination practices.
  3. Analyze power system studies such as fault current analysis and equipment protection reviews, utilizing recognized industry methodologies.
  4. Evaluate and critique the application of protective relays (SEL, GE, or equivalent microprocessor-based relays) in medium voltage environments.
  5. Develop detailed, well-structured written responses and rationales explaining your analysis and recommendations.

  7. Support the creation of realistic, diverse scenarios that reflect U.S. distribution-utility or industrial standards for training and validation purposes.

  2. Strong background in protective relaying, relay settings, power system analysis, and device coordination.
  3. Proficiency with SEL, GE, or standard microprocessor relays and associated software.
  4. Advanced skill in power system modeling tools such as ETAP, ASPEN, or CAPE.
  5. Ability to synthesize and communicate complex technical concepts clearly in both written and verbal formats.
  6. Demonstrated attention to detail and analytical rigor when reviewing technical materials and data sets.
  7. Previous experience validating or creating technical documentation, protection settings, or relay coordination studies is highly regarded.

Role: Engineering PhD


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $80–95/hour

Duration: Short-term pilot — approximately 2–3 weeks

Project kickoff: Ideally end of week( November 8th)

Location: Fully remote

You’ll need: PhD or PhD candidate in electrical, mechanical, chemical, industrial, or aerospace engineering

Your tasks: Build technical problems from real engineering workflows and define what makes an answer correct


This is a short pilot, roughly 2–3 weeks, focused on real engineering workflows: the problems you’d actually encounter in your research or practice, not textbook exercises. You’ll build those problems, provide the correct analysis, and define what separates a right answer from one that only looks right.


What you’ll do

  1. Design technical problems drawn from real engineering work in your field, with realistic constraints and supporting data.
  2. Provide the correct solution and walk through the reasoning that gets there.
  3. Define objective criteria for correctness, so another engineer reviewing the work would reach the same verdict.
  4. Review problems built by other contributors for technical accuracy and soundness of method.
  5. Flag problems that turn out to be ambiguous or ungradable rather than submitting them.

What we’re looking for

  1. PhD, or PhD candidate, in electrical, mechanical, chemical, industrial, or aerospace engineering.
  2. Degree from a strong research institution is preferred.
  3. Hands-on research or practice experience — problems you worked on yourself, not ones you read about.
  4. Able to explain why an answer is correct clearly enough that another engineer could verify it.

Role Title: AI Agent Evaluator

Role Type: Contractor

Location: U.S based


Opportunity Snapshot


Pay: $25-45/hour

Time per task: ~1.5 hours per run (evidence and scoring included)

Project kickoff: Monday, October 12

Onboarding: Today (Fri), Saturday, or Sunday, so you’re ready to start Monday October 10th

You’ll need: An active personal popular AI account (Free, Go, or Plus; not Pro), an active personal and a smartphone that can screen record

Your tasks: Run everyday errands with two AI agents, approve key steps, screen record, and score the results


About the role


AI agents are starting to handle real-life errands: paying bills, booking trips, doing the groceries. We want to know how well they actually do it, from the point of view of a real user. That’s you.

You’ll test two AI agents side by side, using your own accounts on your phone, and tell us what worked, what didn’t, and how it felt.


What you’ll do

  1. Run real-life scenarios: bills, returns, email follow-ups, bookings, shopping, groceries, travel, family logistics, outings, and forms
  2. Approve or stop the agent at key steps
  3. Screen record every attempt
  4. Score each run on completion, quality, control issues, satisfaction, and time
  5. Share clear written feedback on the agent experience

Who we’re looking for

  1. US-based, with a Bachelor’s degree
  2. Someone who already uses AI in daily life
  3. 2-3 years of experience, preferably in engineering, business management, or office/operations
  4. Detail-oriented, great at following instructions and documenting each step
  5. Clear written communication
  6. Generalists welcome, domain experts preferred
  7. No coding or AI background needed


Why you’ll like it

  1. Get paid to use the AI tools you already use
  2. Work entirely from your phone, on your schedule
  3. Have a direct say in how next-generation AI agents get built and improved


How the selection process works

  1. Apply
  2. Complete the screening questions
  3. Interview: 15-30 minutes max
  4. Profile review: if everything looks good, we present you to the client
  5. Onboarding: our Talent Ops team will contact you to get you started

AI agents are starting to handle real-life errands: paying bills, booking trips, doing the groceries. We want to know how well they actually do it, from the point of view of a real user. That’s you.

You’ll test two AI agents side by side, using your own accounts on your phone, and tell us what worked, what didn’t, and how it felt.

###

### What you’ll do

- Run real-life scenarios: bills, returns, email follow-ups, bookings, shopping, groceries, travel, family logistics, outings, and forms

- Approve or stop the agent at key steps

- Screen record every attempt

- Score each run on completion, quality, control issues, satisfaction, and time

- Share clear written feedback on the agent experience

### Who we’re looking for

- US-based, with a Bachelor’s degree

- Someone who already uses AI in daily life

- 2-3 years of experience, preferably in engineering, business management, or office/operations

- Detail-oriented, great at following instructions and documenting each step

- Clear written communication

- Generalists welcome, domain experts preferred

- No coding or AI background needed

###

### Why you’ll like it

- Get paid to use the AI tools you already use

- Work entirely from your phone, on your schedule

- Have a direct say in how next-generation AI agents get built and improved

###

### How the selection process works

- Apply

- Complete the screening questions

- Interview: 15-30 minutes max

- Profile review: if everything looks good, we present you to the client

- Onboarding: our Talent Ops team will contact you to get you started

Role Title: Music & Sound Annotation Expert


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is engaging Music & Sound Annotation Experts to contribute to a customer's project at the forefront of music and audio technology.

Your ears are the ground truth. You'll listen to short field recordings and document exactly what's audible — instruments, tempo, key, background sounds, crowd reactions — through a structured web platform built for this project. Later phases involve grading AI model answers against what you actually heard.


What you'll do

  1. Listen to 30–90 second field recordings (headphones, your own quiet workspace) and complete structured annotations: which instruments are present, tempo and key, timestamps of background events (traffic, sirens, applause), scene details
  2. Compare paired recordings of the same song captured at different locations and judge what stayed the same and what changed
  3. In later phases: review AI model descriptions of clips and mark what's correct, wrong, or invented, with a brief written explanation
  4. Attend a paid onboarding/calibration session and a short weekly sync


Who we're looking for (any of these backgrounds)

  1. Working or gigging musicians, session players, producers, or mixing engineers
  2. Music educators, ear-training instructors, band/choir directors, conservatory students or graduates
  3. Location sound recordists, sound designers, foley artists, or podcast/documentary audio editors


Requirements

  1. 3+ years of hands-on music or audio experience
  2. Strong analytical listening: you can pick individual instruments out of a busy, noisy, real-world mix — not just studio recordings
  3. Can identify tempo (within a few BPM) and musical key (relative pitch with a reference is fine)
  4. Comfortable with detail-oriented, repetitive annotation work in a web platform — dropdowns, timestamps, short structured notes
  5. Clear written English for brief, evidence-based notes (e.g., "accordion enters around 0:12")
  6. Quality headphones, quiet workspace, reliable internet
  7. Available 20–25 hrs/week for the engagement window
