Role Title: Domain Contributor - Evaluation Specialist


Role Type: Contractor (~15 hrs/week)


Location: Remote


micro1 is engaging Domain Contributor - Evaluation Specialists to support an internal project evaluating and improving advanced AI models. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. Flexible, pay-per-task work across history, law, finance, journalism, and tech, for experts with prior AI training experience.


Scope of Work

  1. Design nuanced, domain-specific tasks that probe AI model limits and surface reasoning flaws.
  2. Author questions and scenarios demanding deep subject knowledge, beyond general understanding.
  3. Assess AI-generated outputs, validating accuracy against authoritative, primary sources in your area of expertise.
  4. Document clear rationales for model shortcomings, specifying missed reasoning, source errors, or nuances.
  5. Apply detailed task guidelines and evaluation rubrics consistently to each submission.
  6. Submit completed deliverables independently on a rolling basis, meeting project requirements for written and verbal clarity.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Proven hands-on experience with AI model training, annotation, RLHF, or evaluation.
  2. Deep expertise in a core domain: history, archival or library science, law (paralegal, legal academic, compliance), finance (equity research, PE/VC, forensic accounting), journalism, or technology/industry history.
  3. Advanced research skills with a track record of verifying complex claims against authoritative sources.
  4. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills to articulate findings and feedback.
  5. Demonstrated ability to precisely follow detailed instructions and evaluation frameworks.
  6. Background in adversarial or “stomp the model” task design is advantageous.
  7. Graduate-level research, experience at a Fortune 100 company, or professional fluency in a non-English language a plus.


Compensation Structure

Compensation is output-based; experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required to complete work may vary depending on the expert’s experience and workflow. Minimum submission requirements apply. Experts must submit a minimum of tasks per week.


Start Timeline & Availability

We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts ready to jump in right away. If selected, we expect you to start your first tasks within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.

Job Title: Derivatives Counsel (ISDA Specialist)


Job Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Job Summary: We are seeking seasoned Derivatives Counsels for a part-time role at the forefront of legal AI. This opportunity is for elite lawyers who want to help shape how advanced AI is trained, evaluated, and applied in real-world legal work, especially those with deep experience drafting, reviewing, negotiating, and redlining ISDA Master Agreements and related derivatives documentation.


In this role, you will review, assess, and contribute to contract redlining workflows used to train and evaluate state-of-the-art AI models. Your work will directly improve how these systems identify risk and interpret derivatives documentation to create tools with improved precision and legal judgment.


Key Responsibilities:

  1. Perform simulated negotiations and redlining exercises on ISDA Master Agreements.
  2. Review and assess AI responses to derivatives contract scenarios, providing expert feedback to improve model performance and output precision.
  3. Create objective evaluation frameworks and grading criteria to assess AI performance on derivatives documentation tasks with rigor and consistency.
  4. Collaborate with product and research teams to refine data, guidelines, and best practices for AI-driven contract review solutions.


Required Skills and Qualifications:

  1. Minimum of 3 years of experience in derivatives documentation, with hands-on negotiation of ISDA Master Agreements, LPAs, CSAs and other types of commercial agreements.
  2. Deep familiarity with key ISDA provisions, including events of default, termination events, close-out netting, and collateral terms.
  3. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with meticulous attention to detail.
  4. Strong analytical capabilities and ability to translate legal expertise into actionable feedback for AI systems.
  5. Experience working with cross-disciplinary teams in fast-paced environments.


Preferred Qualifications:

  1. Prior exposure to AI, legal tech, or training initiatives.


Why Join:

  1. This is an opportunity to work at the intersection of law and technology.
  2. You will help define how AI is developed for a new generation of legal practitioners.
  3. You will apply your experience in a high-impact research environment.


Compensation Structure:


Compensation is task-based, meaning experts are paid per completed task that meets the project specifications. The average handling time (AHT) is approximately 3.5 hours per task, and the effective hourly rate will depend on the number of tasks completed and successfully signed off.

Role Title: Consular Officer / Passport Specialist


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Time Commitment: 20-30 hours/week, short-term project


micro1 is looking for former Consular Officers and Passport Specialists to help evaluate and improve AI systems on passport and citizenship topics. You’ll use your State Department experience to check that questions sound like real applicants and that answers are correct on complex cases. Accuracy comes first. No AI experience is needed; your domain knowledge is what matters.


Scope of Work

  1. Review sample passport and citizenship questions and flag any that don’t sound like what real people ask.
  2. Write rubrics that define a correct, complete answer for complex cases, such as lost, stolen, or damaged passports, name changes, and citizenship documentation.
  3. Cover situations involving minors, custody, and applicants born or living abroad in your rubrics.
  4. Evaluate AI-generated answers against your rubrics, flagging errors, omissions, and outdated guidance.
  5. Share clear written feedback with the project team, working asynchronously.


Required Qualifications

  1. Former State Department experience in a passport agency (Passport Specialist/Adjudicator) or consular section (Consular Officer)
  2. 1+ years adjudicating or advising on passport or citizenship matters
  3. Working knowledge of citizenship and nationality rules and passport eligibility
  4. US-based
  5. Able to start quickly and commit 20-30 hours/week
  6. Clear, precise writing


Nice to Have

  1. Experience with document fraud detection
  2. Experience with name change and identity documentation cases
  3. Experience creating guides, FAQs, or training materials
  4. Experience helping a diverse range of applicants, including non-English-speaking customers

Role Title: Medical Chart Reviewer


Role Type: Contractor


Location: US - Remote


micro1 is engaging Medical Chart Reviewers (CCS / CIC / CPC certified, or RN / clinical background) to contribute their expertise to a dynamic project for a valued customer. In this role, you’ll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required, your domain knowledge is what matters.


Scope of Work

  1. Review and audit medical charts, including admission notes, progress notes, operative reports, consults, lab and imaging results, and discharge summaries, to verify the accuracy and completeness of documentation and assigned codes.
  2. Validate diagnosis and procedure coding, sequencing, Present on Admission (POA) indicators, and MS-DRG assignment against the clinical documentation, identifying under-coding, over-coding, and missed CCs and MCCs.
  3. Apply clinical and coding standards, including the ICD-10-CM/PCS Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting, AHA Coding Clinic guidance, and clinical validation criteria, while flagging documentation gaps and query opportunities.
  4. Collaborate with project stakeholders using both written and verbal communication to clarify requirements, resolve documentation ambiguities, and ensure data integrity.
  5. Deliver high-quality feedback on charts, coding guidelines, and complex cases to support project workflow improvements and enhance AI model understanding.
  6. Ensure accuracy and completeness of all review findings per current best practices and coding standards.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Active AHIMA Certified Coding Specialist (CCS), AAPC Certified Inpatient Coder (CIC), AAPC Certified Professional Coder (CPC), or an RN / clinical credential with chart review or CDI experience.
  2. Thorough expertise in ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS, and MS-DRG methodology, with hands-on experience in chart review, coding audit, or clinical documentation improvement (CDI).
  3. Experience reviewing charts in diverse settings, such as acute care, teaching hospitals, specialty units, surgical, trauma, oncology, cardiology, and transplant cases.
  4. Proficiency in reviewing various types of clinical documentation and identifying discrepancies or complex coding challenges.
  5. Strong written and verbal communication skills, demonstrating meticulous attention to detail and clarity.
  6. Access to current ICD-10-CM and ICD-10-PCS code sets, Official Coding Guidelines, and MS-DRG grouper tools.

Job Type: Full-time


Location: Remote


Job Summary: In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.


Key Responsibilities

  1. Design, build, and manage robust data workflows for accurate annotation, collection, processing, and analysis.

Role Title: Contracts Attorney


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote (US Based)


micro1 is engaging Contracts Attorneys to contribute to a confidential project at the intersection of law and AI. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters. The work draws directly on day-to-day commercial contracting practice: reviewing agreements, marking up drafts, and applying company policy positions the way in-house counsel would.


Scope of Work

  1. Review and redline commercial agreements, including MSAs, NDAs, DPAs, and similar documents, in accordance with established playbooks and policies.
  2. Analyze drafts to identify key issues and determine applicable company positions and acceptable fallback outcomes.
  3. Draft clear, reasoned written explanations detailing the rationale behind each redline or revision.
  4. Apply advanced contract drafting, negotiation, and technology transactions knowledge to real-world legal documents.
  5. Collaborate with the project team to ensure consistency of standards and interpretations throughout the engagement.
  6. Maintain meticulous attention to detail and uphold high standards of legal writing and contract review quality.
  7. Work independently within a remote, deadline-driven project environment.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Juris Doctor (JD) from an accredited law school and active bar admission in a U.S. jurisdiction.
  2. Minimum of 4 years' experience in transactional practice at a law firm or as an in-house attorney, focusing on contract drafting, review, and negotiation.
  3. Deep familiarity with commonly negotiated commercial provisions, such as limitation of liability, indemnification, confidentiality, and data protection.
  4. Proven ability to synthesize complex legal concepts and deliver clear, actionable written analyses.
  5. Demonstrated sound judgment and a high level of accuracy in contract review and interpretation.
  6. Expertise in technology transactions considered a strong plus.
  7. Adaptability and drive to contribute to a high-impact, innovative legal project in a confidential setting.

Role Title: Postal Clerk


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Time Commitment: 15-25 hours/week, short-term project


micro1 is looking for Postal Clerks to help evaluate and improve AI systems on postal service topics. You’ll use your front-counter experience to check that questions sound like real customers and that answers are correct and useful. Accuracy comes first. No AI experience is needed; your domain knowledge is what matters.


Scope of Work

  1. Review sample postal questions and flag any that don’t sound like what real customers ask.
  2. Write rubrics that define a correct, complete answer on mail classes, shipping options, postage, fees, and shipping labels.
  3. Cover package tracking, missing or damaged mail, change of address and mail forwarding, and international mailing and customs forms in your rubrics.
  4. Evaluate AI-generated answers against your rubrics, flagging errors, omissions, and outdated guidance.
  5. Share clear written feedback with the project team, working asynchronously.


Required Qualifications

  1. Current, former, or retired USPS frontline experience (postal clerk, sales and service associate, or retail associate)
  2. 1+ years helping customers in person at a post office counter
  3. Working knowledge of mail classes, shipping options, postage, tracking, and change of address
  4. US-based
  5. Able to start quickly and commit 15-25 hours/week
  6. Clear, precise writing


Not a fit: Mail carrier, mail processing, or private shipping store experience alone


Nice to Have

  1. Experience with international mail and customs documentation
  2. Experience handling missing or damaged mail claims
  3. Experience creating guides, FAQs, or training materials
  4. Experience helping a diverse range of customers, including rural and non-English-speaking communities

Job Type: Contractor (~15 hrs a week)


Location: Remote


Schedule: Flexible, you pick the hours and days (including weekends if desired)


Job Summary: In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.


You'll create realistic, interesting and challenging coding tasks for AI to solve involving feature implementation and bug fixes, and implement deterministic verifiers that accept reasonable valid solutions and reject everything else.



What we're looking for

  1. Strong backend experience in Java, Node.js, Go, Rust, Typescript, Python, C++ or similar
  2. A track record building scalable services and APIs
  3. Comfort with debugging, performance work and automated testing
  4. Solid code review instincts
  5. A strong testing background is a big plus — experience designing test strategy, building and maintaining large test suites, diagnosing flaky tests, or raising the testing bar on a team.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Proven experience in backend development, with a track record of delivering high-quality and performant projects.
  2. Demonstrated success in identifying and resolving software bugs and system bottlenecks.
  3. Experience with codebase refactoring and implementing complex features in large-scale applications.
  4. Strong understanding of algorithms, data structures, and foundational computer science concepts.
  5. Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and technical communication skills.


A note on the process: our interview and assessment stages are designed to see how you think, so we ask that you complete them without outside assistance. The same applies once you're on the project — the value of the work comes from your own judgment.


Process:

  1. Apply to the role, filling out the screening questions
  2. Complete AI Interview (approx. 30 minutes)
  3. Technical Assessment (Tentative)
  4. Hiring Manager review


Compensation Structure

Compensation is output-based; experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required to complete work may vary depending on the expert’s experience and workflow. Minimum submission requirements apply. Experts must submit a minimum of tasks per week.


Start Timeline & Availability

We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts ready to jump in right away. If selected, we expect you to start your first tasks within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.

Role Title: Legal Citation Specialist (Law Students)


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot


Pay: $50–80/hour

You’ll need: Current or recent law school enrollment, hands-on Bluebook experience, and law journal or law review editing experience

Your tasks: Review citation-checking rubrics and build sample cite-checking tasks


Job Description

micro1 is engaging law students and recent law graduates with law journal experience to support a legal citation project. If you’ve spent time cite-checking for a law review or journal, this is that skill applied to a new context. No prior AI experience is required — your Bluebook fluency and editorial judgment are what matter.


Scope of Work

  1. Review existing Bluebook and pincite grading rubrics, and flag rules that are unclear, incomplete, or would be applied inconsistently by different editors.
  2. Identify edge cases the rubrics don’t currently cover and recommend how they should be handled.
  3. Create sample cite-checking tasks: source material paired with citations containing realistic errors, along with the correct answer and an explanation of the rule involved.
  4. Build tasks across a range of citation types and difficulty levels, from straightforward formatting errors to subtle pincite and source-support problems.
  5. Apply Bluebook rules consistently across all submissions.
  6. Flag ambiguous cases to project coordinators instead of resolving them silently.
  7. Deliver assigned work on schedule and at the required quality level.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Current law student (2L, 3L) or recent JD graduate.
  2. Law review or law journal experience, ideally including a cite-checking or source-collection role.
  3. Strong working knowledge of The Bluebook, including pincites, short forms, signals, and parentheticals.
  4. Able to explain why a citation is wrong, not just that it is — the reasoning matters as much as the correction.
  5. Careful and consistent across long sessions of detailed review work.
  6. Comfortable working independently and meeting deadlines without close supervision.
  7. Experience as a journal editor, articles editor, or executive editor is a plus.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview— this is how we showcase your skills to the client
  3. Profile review by the hiring team
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

extra.html:
報酬：$12 〜 $21 / 時間

元の求人ページ（英語）：At Home Video Recorder (Japan)

必須スキル

動画撮影、デバイスのセットアップと操作、細部への注意力、手先の器用さ、複雑な指示に従う力、継続的な改善、文章でのコミュニケーション、口頭でのコミュニケーション、フィードバックの反映、反復作業への忍耐力


micro1について

micro1は、AIラボや企業による基盤モデルおよびAIエージェントのトレーニングを支援するデータラボです。LLMの能力向上のための最先端の評価および強化学習環境に加え、企業環境におけるAIエージェントのモニタリングと改善のためのコンテキスト評価を提供しています。

当社のAIリクルーティングエージェントは、高品質なトレーニングデータを迅速に生産できるデータプラットフォームのために、各分野の専門家を発掘・審査しています。当社の研究は、専門家レベルのデータの作成が最も難しく、かつ高度なモデル性能にとって最も価値の高い、専門性の高い領域（法律、医療、金融、コーディングなど）に及びます。当社のパイプライン・パフォーマンス・システムにより、品質とスピードの両立を実現しています。

雇用形態：業務委託（コントラクター）

勤務地：リモート（日本在住の方）


業務概要

次世代のパーソナルロボットのトレーニングにご協力ください。UMIグリッパー（ロボットの手を模倣しながら、自然な動作で作業を行えるウェアラブルデバイス）を使用して、日常的な家事作業の高品質な動画デモンストレーションを撮影していただきます。あなたのデモンストレーションは、ロボットが実際の家庭で作業する方法を学ぶためのトレーニングデータとなります。


主な業務内容

  1. UMIグリッパー（ウェアラブルデバイス）を使用し、日常的な家事作業について、仕様に準拠した高品質な動画デモンストレーションを撮影・提出する。
  2. すべての撮影がプロジェクトの厳格な基準を満たすよう、タスクごとの詳細な指示に従う。
  3. 担当レビュアーからのフィードバックを確認し、データ品質向上のために作業方法を継続的に改善する。
  4. 作業中に実際の手の動きを正確に再現できるよう、撮影機材およびUMIグリッパーのセットアップと操作を行う。
  5. クライアントのプロジェクトチームと、文章・口頭の両方で、積極的かつ明確にコミュニケーションを取る。
  6. 承認データの最低要件を満たすため、毎週安定したワークフローを維持する。


必須スキル・応募資格

  1. 細部への鋭い注意力と、複雑な仕様に正確に従う能力。
  2. 手先の器用さ、およびさまざまな家庭環境で精密な身体作業を行った経験。
  3. 専用デバイスや撮影機材の操作・装着・セットアップに抵抗がないこと。
  4. フィードバックを取り入れ、作業プロセスや成果物を継続的に改善できること。
  5. 優れた文章力・口頭でのコミュニケーション能力（迅速なフィードバックのやり取りに前向きであること）。
  6. 設備の整った日本の住環境（キッチン、居住スペース、一般的な生活用品）を常時利用できること。
  7. 自宅の安定した高速インターネット回線で、大容量の動画ファイルをアップロードできること。
  8. 本業務ではVRヘッドセットを長時間使用します。通常の業務の一環として、長時間の装着に抵抗がない方が対象です。


歓迎スキル・経験

Role Title: Lawyer

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote, US-based only


micro1 is seeking experienced U.S.-licensed Lawyers across a wide range of legal practice areasto contribute to a project focused on improving AI systems' legal reasoning, accuracy, and judgment.


In this role, you will apply your legal expertise to evaluate complex legal scenarios, review AI-generated legal work, and provide expert feedback to help train advanced AI models.


Scope of Work


  1. Analyze legal scenarios involving litigation, corporate transactions, and regulatory or compliance matters to identify key legal issues, risks, and relevant legal principles.
  2. Review and evaluate AI-generated legal analyses, arguments, contracts, and other legal documents for accuracy, completeness, and sound reasoning.
  3. Identify legal errors, unsupported conclusions, missing information, and weaknesses in legal reasoning.
  4. Apply professional legal judgment to complex or ambiguous situations, considering relevant laws, facts, and competing interpretations.
  5. Provide clear, structured feedback and corrections to improve the quality and reliability of AI-generated legal outputs.


Required Qualifications


  1. Juris Doctor (J.D.) degree from a U.S. law school.
  2. Active bar license in at least one U.S. state or the District of Columbia.
  3. More than 3 years of substantive post-J.D. legal practice.**
  4. Strong legal reasoning, issue-spotting, legal writing, and document review skills.
  5. Excellent written English communication and attention to detail.
  6. Ability to work independently in a remote contractor environment.


Preferred Qualifications


  1. Experience in any legal practice area, including litigation, corporate, commercial, employment, personal injury, criminal, family, immigration, insurance, intellectual property, healthcare, securities, real estate, tax, privacy, environmental, or regulatory law.
  2. Experience reviewing complex legal documents, identifying substantive errors, or evaluating competing legal arguments.
  3. Familiarity with legal technology, AI-assisted research, or AI evaluation is a plus, but not required.

Role Title: Physics Expert (PhD / Postdoc)

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote (Worldwide)

Schedule: 10-15+ hours a week, Fully Flexible (Can accommodate working after hours/weekends)


micro1 is engaging Physics Experts (PhD / Postdoc) to contribute deep scientific knowledge and problem-solving skills to a high-impact customer project. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems.


Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.


Scope of Work

  1. Solve advanced physics problems from your specialization, delivering rigorous, well-documented derivations and analyses.
  2. Produce technically precise, clearly written solutions, detailing all assumptions, approximations, and final results using LaTeX mathematical notation.
  3. Utilize SymPy, Python, and Jupyter for symbolic or numerical verification and clear computational workflows where relevant.
  4. Identify and articulate subtleties in problem statements, including special cases, boundary conditions, and dimensional consistency.
  5. Flag ambiguities in project materials, proposing well-reasoned interpretations and clarifications as needed.
  6. Iterate on submitted solutions in response to feedback from project reviewers, ensuring corrections are cleanly integrated.
  7. Uphold rigorous standards in documentation and reproducibility consistent with professional research practice.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. PhD in physics or advanced-stage PhD candidacy, with active research experience in a relevant subfield.
  2. Research expertise in one or more of: High Energy Physics, Mathematical Physics, Biophysics, Statistical Physics, Condensed Matter (including moiré systems, magnetism, PXP/Rydberg), AMO/Quantum Optics, Gravitation, Cosmology, Astrophysics, Quantum Information, or Optical Properties of Materials.
  3. 2–5 recent representative publications (past ~5 years) in your field, with accessible arXiv or DOI records.
  4. Proficiency with LaTeX for presenting mathematics, and with SymPy, Python, and Jupyter for computational work; willingness to indicate areas for further support if needed.
  5. Demonstrated excellence in written technical communication, with a track record of producing clear, precise, and well-argued scientific outputs.
  6. Strong analytical skills, able to isolate key physical principles and provide nuanced solutions to complex problems.
  7. Availability to engage with the project consistently over an 8–10 week period (approx. 10 hours/week).

Job Title: STEM Expert – Biology & Bioinformatics (PhD)


Job Type: Contractor


Location: Remote(Worldwide)


Job Summary: In this role, you’ll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input.


Key Responsibilities:

  1. Design, evaluate, and critique biology, bioinformatics, and computational biology workflows to support AI benchmarking initiatives.
  2. Provide expert-level insights on genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and other biological data analysis pipelines.
  3. Assess and optimize pipeline parameters, tool configurations, and statistical methods for accuracy and reproducibility.
  4. Analyze biological datasets (e.g., NGS, RNA-seq, single-cell, variant calling, protein structure) and provide actionable recommendations.
  5. Leverage domain knowledge to guide the development and validation of biology-related AI models and tools.
  6. Communicate complex scientific concepts clearly, both in writing and verbally, to technical and non-technical collaborators.
  7. Document findings, methodologies, and best practices to ensure knowledge transfer across the customer’s team.


Areas of Expertise (we welcome applicants from any of the following):

  1. Genomics & NGS analysis
  2. Transcriptomics & single-cell analysis
  3. Proteomics & structural biology
  4. Molecular & cell biology
  5. Systems biology & biological network analysis
  6. Drug discovery & computational pharmacology
  7. Biostatistics & machine learning applied to biology


Required Skills and Qualifications:

  1. PhD in biology, bioinformatics, computational biology, genomics, or a closely related STEM field, or equivalent industry/research experience.
  2. Professional written and spoken English (C1 or higher).
  3. Deep expertise in at least one of the areas listed above, with hands-on experience analyzing real biological data.
  4. Proficiency in Python and/or R for scientific analysis, plus experience with standard tools in your subfield (e.g., BLAST, samtools, GATK, Bioconductor, Biopython).
  5. Strong statistical, quantitative, and analytical reasoning skills.
  6. Outstanding written and verbal communication abilities, with the ability to clearly document and explain technical concepts.
  7. Track record of rigorous scientific problem-solving in complex biological domains.


Preferred Qualifications:

  1. Experience building reproducible workflows (Nextflow, Snakemake) and working in Linux/command-line environments.
  2. Experience with AI/ML-assisted biology workflows or benchmarking.
  3. Peer-reviewed publications, patents, or contributions to open-source bioinformatics software.

Job Summary: In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.


As an expert you will be creating Reinforcement Learning Environments which test an AI model’s ability to solve complex competitive programming problems. You will be tasked with creating a unique custom problem absent from all existing online judges, creating a reference solution and creating a robust test suite.


Key Responsibilities:

  1. Design and implement checkers for competitive programming problems with multiple valid outputs, ensuring accuracy and robustness.
  2. Evaluate and validate participant submissions against complex problem statements sourced from platforms like Codeforces.
  3. Collaborate with the customer's team to fine-tune problem requirements and clarify ambiguous scenarios.

  5. Document checker logic and communicate intricacies or edge cases in both written and verbal form.

  7. Stay updated with evolving competitive programming standards and incorporate best practices into checker development.


Required Skills and Qualifications:

  1. Expertise in competitive programming and coding problem analysis.
  2. Advanced proficiency in C++ for implementing robust checker solutions.
  3. Strong analytical abilities to interpret complex problem constraints and multiple solution paths.
  4. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; ability to articulate technical details clearly.
  5. Meticulous attention to detail in code validation and output consistency.
  6. Experience working independently in a remote, collaborative environment.
  7. Commitment to producing high-quality, well-documented code under tight deadlines.


Preferred Qualifications:

  1. Prior experience as a problem setter, tester, or checker on major competitive programming platforms.



Compensation Structure

Compensation is output-based; experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required to complete work may vary depending on the expert’s experience and workflow. Minimum submission requirements apply. Experts must submit a minimum of tasks per week.


Start Timeline & Availability

We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts ready to jump in right away. If selected, we expect you to start your first tasks within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.

Role Title: Senior Technical Documentation, Parts and Annotation Specialist


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is engaging Senior Technical Documentation, Parts and Annotation Specialists to contribute their deep domain expertise to a customer's innovative project. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.


Scope of Work

  1. Transform engineering drawings and bills of materials (BOMs) into precise, dependency-correct assembly procedures suitable for technical manuals.
  2. Identify, verify, and document industrial replacement parts and components based on photos, nameplates, and manufacturer or distributor catalogs, ensuring accurate fitment and application details.
  3. Interpret production patterns, markers, and cutting-room plans for apparel or industrial fabrication, verifying layout efficiency and technical correctness.
  4. Conduct quality assurance reviews on annotated image batches, adjudicating label accuracy against established project ontologies and annotation guidelines.
  5. Produce clear, defensible rationales for decisions and recommendations, capturing expert thought processes for model training purposes.
  6. Review and refine real-world documents, photos, patterns, or annotation data, delivering outputs at the standard expected from a senior practitioner in your field.
  7. Collaborate remotely with project coordinators, submitting deliverables through digital platforms within agreed project timelines.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Minimum 5 years of experience in one or more of the following domains: mechanical technical writing, industrial parts/application analysis, production pattern planning, or computer vision annotation quality assurance.
  2. Exceptional proficiency with interpreting engineering drawings, BOMs, and technical documentation, or demonstrated expertise with parts identification and catalog research.
  3. Strong analytical, visual, and spatial reasoning abilities, particularly in pattern interpretation or assembly process documentation.
  4. Proven track record of producing clear, structured, and accurate records, reports, or manuals to industry standards.

Location: Remote, United States

Commitment: Part-time, project-based

Compensation: $60–$80 USD per hour


About the opportunity


micro1 is seeking experienced Federal Contract Specialists to contribute their federal acquisition expertise to a customer project focused on AI evaluation.


In this role, you'll draw on your hands-on experience with federal contracting to develop realistic acquisition scenarios, create detailed reference answers, and evaluate work produced by other subject matter experts. No prior experience in AI is required. Your federal contracting expertise is what matters.


What you'll do


  1. Develop realistic federal contracting scenarios based on your hands-on acquisition experience, reflecting the complexities of government procurement.
  2. Create detailed, accurate reference answers that demonstrate sound contracting decisions and established federal acquisition practices.
  3. Review scenarios and reference answers developed by other subject matter experts, identifying inaccuracies and providing constructive feedback.
  4. Ensure all deliverables align with current Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) requirements and applicable federal contracting standards.
  5. Apply your knowledge of pre-award and post-award contracting procedures to assess the accuracy and realism of project materials.
  6. Collaborate asynchronously with project coordinators and fellow specialists to review deliverables and maintain quality standards.
  7. Contribute professional insights that strengthen the accuracy, relevance, and effectiveness of AI evaluation materials.


Required qualifications


  1. Current or previous professional experience in federal contracting, including OPM series GS-1102 or equivalent federal acquisition experience.
  2. Strong understanding of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and the federal acquisition lifecycle, including pre-award and post-award activities.
  3. Ability to apply federal contracting knowledge to realistic acquisition scenarios and explain decisions clearly.
  4. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex contracting concepts accurately.
  5. Based in the United States, with reliable internet connectivity for remote participation.


Preferred qualifications


  1. Experience developing or reviewing federal acquisition scenarios, training materials, or evaluation content.
  2. Current or previous experience holding a contracting officer warrant.
  3. Professional certifications such as Federal Acquisition Certification in Contracting (FAC-C) or Defense Acquisition Workforce Improvement Act (DAWIA) contracting certification.


Engagement details

  1. Compensation: $60–$80 USD per hour.
  2. Engagement type:Independent contractor.
  3. Commitment: Part-time, project-based.
  4. Location: Remote, United States.


Application process


After submitting your application, you'll be invited to complete an AI interview designed to assess your federal contracting experience, knowledge of acquisition procedures, and ability to apply your expertise to realistic contracting scenarios.


About micro1

micro1 is a data lab that connects professionals with opportunities to apply their expertise to customer projects. Through our extended network, contributors bring their knowledge and judgment to projects with their own scope, requirements, and engagement terms.

Role Title: Intelligence Analyst


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is engaging Intelligence Analysts to contribute to a customer-facing project focused on evaluating and advancing artificial intelligence capabilities. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.


Scope of Work

  1. Develop and map analytic cases to defined taxonomies across multiple evaluation areas, ensuring comprehensive coverage of relevant intelligence scenarios.
  2. Author complex test cases designed to evaluate model performance on source handling, analytic rigor, and nuanced uncertainty expression.
  3. Assess and grade AI-generated responses based on criteria such as reasoning, source use, recognition of limitations, and practical utility.
  4. Identify and flag instances where legitimate analytic exploration is over-refused by the model, providing clear documentation and feedback.
  5. Document edge cases and analytic disagreements, supporting continuous improvement of evaluation methodologies.
  6. Collaborate with project leads to refine procedures for source evaluation and confidence-level assignment.
  7. Contribute insights to help calibrate analytic standards and enhance the overall quality of AI system benchmarks.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Demonstrated all-source analytic experience or deep expertise in a specific analytic discipline, ideally with a civilian-IC background.
  2. Strong proficiency in source evaluation, confidence-level assessment, and established analytic standards.
  3. Experience in teaching, mentoring, or leading analytic reviews, with a record of fostering analytic rigor.
  4. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with a focus on clarity and precision.
  5. Ability to identify and articulate nuanced model limitations and over-refusal scenarios.
  6. Familiarity with structured analytic techniques and intelligence tradecraft standards.
  7. Previous participation in AI evaluation or model assessment initiatives is a plus.

extra.html:
Role Title: Procurement & Vendor Management Expert


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: Up to $90/hour equivalent.

Time per task: ~10 hours per task

Location: Fully remote — no geographic restrictions. Strong English required (B2 minimum, C1 preferred)

Next step: Complete the role-specific AI interview — it’s how your expertise gets in front of the client

Your tasks: Design realistic, multi-step procurement and vendor management tasks with objective criteria for grading the output


micro1 is engaging experienced procurement and vendor management practitioners to design the tasks that measure what AI systems can actually do. Your domain knowledge is what matters here — no prior AI experience required.


The work is to turn real procurement workflows into benchmark tasks: realistic, difficult, and gradable against objective criteria. If you’ve built a supplier scorecard, run a weighted bid evaluation, or written a vendor risk framework, that’s exactly the instinct this needs.


Scope of Work

  1. Design multi-step tasks drawn from real procurement work — supplier assessment, bid comparison, vendor risk analysis, contract review — with realistic reference files and clear instructions.
  2. Define objective grading criteria so two qualified reviewers would reach the same verdict on the same output.
  3. Build tasks that require judgment rather than lookup: ones where the right answer depends on reading the materials correctly.
  4. Create or source the supporting materials each task needs: RFP responses, pricing schedules, contracts, SLAs, risk assessments.
  5. Flag tasks that turn out to be ambiguous or ungradable instead of submitting them anyway.
  6. Deliver approved tasks on schedule and at the required quality level.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. 5+ years of hands-on responsibility in procurement, sourcing, supplier assessment, or vendor management — direct ownership of the work, not supervisory-only or adjacent exposure.
  2. Experience creating or applying structured evaluation standards: supplier scorecards, weighted bid criteria, vendor risk frameworks, or category strategies.
  3. Comfortable working across contracts, spreadsheets, and reports at the same time.
  4. CIPS, CPSM or equivalent certification is a plus, but not required.
  5. Strong English, written and spoken — B2 minimum, C1 preferred.
  6. AI or LLM evaluation experience is a plus, but not required.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview for this role — even if you’ve interviewed with us before, a role-specific interview is how we showcase your domain expertise to the client, and it gives you the strongest shot at being selected
  3. Profile review
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

Role Title: Software Engineer (Open Source Contributor)


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Anywhere in the world, remote


Opportunity Snapshot


Pay: $50–100/hour

Time per task: ~15 hours per run

Onboarding: As soon as you’re selected, Talent Ops will send you everything you need to get started

You’ll need: clear open source contributions and a profile to showcase them, such as GitHub (preferably with C++, Python, Java, Go, TypeScript, or Rust). If you don’t, you’ll be assessed through a HackerRank assessment instead.

Your tasks: Build reproducible Reinforcement Learning Environments that test an AI model’s ability to fix code, add features, refactor, and optimize performance - including a golden reference solution for each problem

Bonus: experts who complete the AI interview for this specific role move through the process significantly faster.


We care about your human judgment: our interview and assessment stages are designed to see how you think, so we ask that you complete them on your own, without AI assistants or help from others.



Job Description

In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.


You'll create realistic, interesting and challenging coding tasks for AI to solve involving feature implementation and bug fixes, and implement deterministic verifiers that accept reasonable valid solutions and reject everything else.



What we're looking for

  1. Strong backend experience in Java, Node.js, Go, Rust, Typescript, Python, C++ or similar
  2. A track record building scalable services and APIs
  3. Comfort with debugging, performance work and automated testing
  4. Solid code review instincts


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Proven experience in backend development, with a track record of delivering high-quality and performant projects.
  2. Demonstrated success in identifying and resolving software bugs and system bottlenecks.
  3. Experience with codebase refactoring and implementing complex features in large-scale applications.
  4. Strong understanding of algorithms, data structures, and foundational computer science concepts.
  5. Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and technical communication skills.


Scope of Work

  1. Contribute expert-level code samples, debugging strategies, and development insights in Python3, Java, Rust, Go, C++, or TypeScript.
  2. Analyze, troubleshoot, and resolve complex software defects and performance bottlenecks in diverse codebases.
  3. Implement robust new features, ensuring scalability, maintainability, and adherence to software best practices.
  4. Refactor and optimize legacy code to improve clarity, efficiency, and long-term reliability.
  5. Document technical reasoning, solution approaches, and code decisions to enhance AI training data quality.
  6. Review and validate peer-contributed code and technical submissions for accuracy and clarity.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Significant hands-on expertise in at least one of the following: Python3, Java, Rust, Go, C++, or TypeScript.
  2. Deep understanding of algorithms, data structures, and software engineering principles.
  3. Proven ability to debug complex systems, resolve bugs, and deliver effective optimizations.
  4. Experience with large codebase refactoring and legacy system modernization.
  5. Track record of delivering high-impact features from conception through delivery within cross-functional projects.
  6. Strong documentation and communication skills to articulate technical concepts clearly.
  7. Interest in or curiosity about AI and its technical challenges (previous AI experience not required).


Process:

  1. Apply to the role, filling out the screening questions
  2. Complete AI interview (aprox. 20 minutes)
  3. Technical Assessment (if your GitHub profile doesn’t fully showcase the expertise required for this role)
  4. Hiring Manager review



Compensation Structure

Compensation is output-based; experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required to complete work may vary depending on the expert’s experience and workflow. Minimum submission requirements apply. Experts must submit a minimum of tasks per week.


Start Timeline & Availability

We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts ready to jump in right away. If selected, we expect you to start your first tasks within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.

Role Title: Cyber Threat Intelligence SME


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is engaging Cyber Threat Intelligence SMEs to contribute to a leading-edge customer project focused on evaluating and mapping advanced cyber threat scenarios. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.


Scope of Work

  1. Map cyber threat intelligence (CTI) cases to established taxonomies, especially within the surveillance and privacy evaluation domains.
  2. Author boundary cases illustrating prohibited surveillance, attribution, and intrusion-adjacent requests, helping delineate permissible and impermissible actions.
  3. Evaluate and grade submitted threat responses with special attention to source reliability, analytic reasoning, stated limitations, and actionable utility.
  4. Identify and flag instances of over-refusal, ensuring legitimate threat analysis is not unnecessarily declined.
  5. Document and clarify challenging edge cases involving nation-state operations and other advanced threats.
  6. Provide concise written and verbal feedback to support the continuous improvement of AI threat assessment capabilities.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Substantial experience in cyber threat intelligence, particularly where nation-state operations intersect with advanced cyber threats.
  2. Expertise in distinguishing between legitimate defensive/analytic activities and impermissible offensive or surveillance-focused requests.
  3. Background in threat-actor attribution, APT tracking, or exposure to adversary tactics and techniques.
  4. Demonstrated proficiency in authoring clear, structured written content in English and communicating complex concepts verbally.
  5. Experience mentoring, teaching, or leading professionals in threat intelligence disciplines.
  6. Prior participation in AI system evaluation, red-teaming, or related quality assurance projects is a plus.


Learn More About Our Government & Defense Work


At micro1, we work with government and defense experts to evaluate how advanced AI models perform on real-world tasks.

Our MissionReport benchmark assesses AI-generated military and government reports, highlighting the importance of expert judgment, accuracy, and operational understanding.


Learn more: https://www.micro1.ai/benchmark/mission-report

Role Title: Business Operations Expert


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote, global


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: Up to $90/hour equivalent

Time per task: ~10 hours per task

Location: Fully remote — no geographic restrictions. Strong English required (B2 minimum, C1 preferred)

Next step: Complete the role-specific AI interview — it’s how your expertise gets in front of the client

Your tasks: Design realistic, multi-step business operations tasks with objective criteria for grading the output


micro1 is engaging experienced operations practitioners to design the tasks that measure what AI systems can actually do. Your domain knowledge is what matters here — no prior AI experience required.


The work is to turn real operational workflows into benchmark tasks: realistic, difficult, and gradable against objective criteria. If you’ve written an SOP, built a QA checklist, or trained a team against a standard, that’s the instinct this needs.


Scope of Work

  1. Design multi-step tasks drawn from real operations work — reporting, process design, workflow management — with realistic reference files and clear instructions.
  2. Define objective grading criteria so two qualified reviewers would reach the same verdict on the same output.
  3. Build tasks that require judgment rather than lookup: ones where the right answer depends on reading the materials correctly.
  4. Create or source the supporting materials each task needs: spreadsheets, system exports, process documentation, operational reports.
  5. Flag tasks that turn out to be ambiguous or ungradable instead of submitting them anyway.
  6. Deliver approved tasks on schedule and at the required quality level.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. 5+ years of hands-on responsibility in business operations, operations reporting, process design, or workflow management — direct ownership of the work, not supervisory-only or adjacent exposure.
  2. Experience creating or applying structured standards: SOPs, QA checklists, process documentation, service level definitions, or training assessments.
  3. Strong Excel capability and comfort reasoning across multiple documents at once.
  4. Strong English, written and spoken — B2 minimum, C1 preferred.
  5. AI or LLM evaluation experience is a plus, but not required.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview for this role.
  3. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

Role Title: Bluebook Citation Specialist (Law Students & Recent JDs)


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot


Pay: $50–80/hour

You’ll need: Current or recent law school enrollment, hands-on Bluebook experience, and law journal or law review editing experience

Your tasks: Review citation-checking rubrics and build sample cite-checking tasks


Job Description

micro1 is engaging law students and recent law graduates with law journal experience to support a legal citation project. If you’ve spent time cite-checking for a law review or journal, this is that skill applied to a new context. No prior AI experience is required — your Bluebook fluency and editorial judgment are what matter.


Scope of Work

  1. Review existing Bluebook and pincite grading rubrics, and flag rules that are unclear, incomplete, or would be applied inconsistently by different editors.
  2. Identify edge cases the rubrics don’t currently cover and recommend how they should be handled.
  3. Create sample cite-checking tasks: source material paired with citations containing realistic errors, along with the correct answer and an explanation of the rule involved.
  4. Build tasks across a range of citation types and difficulty levels, from straightforward formatting errors to subtle pincite and source-support problems.
  5. Apply Bluebook rules consistently across all submissions.
  6. Flag ambiguous cases to project coordinators instead of resolving them silently.
  7. Deliver assigned work on schedule and at the required quality level.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Current law student (2L, 3L) or recent JD graduate.
  2. Law review or law journal experience, ideally including a cite-checking or source-collection role.
  3. Strong working knowledge of The Bluebook, including pincites, short forms, signals, and parentheticals.
  4. Able to explain why a citation is wrong, not just that it is — the reasoning matters as much as the correction.
  5. Careful and consistent across long sessions of detailed review work.
  6. Comfortable working independently and meeting deadlines without close supervision.
  7. Experience as a journal editor, articles editor, or executive editor is a plus.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview— this is how we showcase your skills to the client
  3. Profile review by the hiring team
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

Role Title: Life Sciences Research Expert (Python)

Pay: $60–$120/hour

Location: Global, fully remote

Job Type: Contractor (~15 hours per week)

Schedule: Flexible—you choose the hours and days you work, including weekends if desired


micro1 is seeking experienced life sciences researchers with strong, hands-on Python skills to contribute to projects focused on evaluating and improving advanced AI systems.


In this role, you will apply your scientific expertise to create, solve, and review challenging research problems within biology and related fields. You will use Python to analyze scientific data, develop reproducible solutions, validate computational results, and identify errors in technical reasoning or code.


Areas of Expertise

We are particularly interested in candidates with expertise in one or more of the following:

  1. Medicine and biomedical science
  2. Computational biology
  3. Neuroscience
  4. Molecular and cellular biology
  5. Biotechnology and bioinformatics
  6. Genetics and genomics
  7. Ecology and evolutionary biology
  8. Biostatistics or biological data science
  9. Etc.

Scope of Work

  1. Create and solve technically rigorous scientific problems within your area of expertise.
  2. Develop reproducible Python-based analyses, models, simulations, or data-processing workflows.
  3. Review scientific solutions and code for correctness, clarity, and completeness.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. PhD, MD, or master’s degree with substantial research experience in a relevant life sciences discipline.
  2. Strong scientific or applied research background demonstrated through publications, thesis work, computational projects, industry research, or equivalent accomplishments.
  3. Practical Python experience for scientific computing, data analysis, modeling, or simulation.
  4. Familiarity with tools such as NumPy, pandas, SciPy, Matplotlib, scikit-learn, Jupyter, or relevant domain-specific libraries.

Process

  1. Apply to the role and complete the screening questions.
  2. Complete an AI interview of approximately 30 minutes.
  3. Complete the hiring manager review.

Compensation Structure

Compensation is output-based. Experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required to complete each task may vary depending on the expert’s experience and workflow.

Minimum submission requirements apply..

Start Timeline & Availability

We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts who are ready to begin immediately. If selected, you will be expected to start your first task within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.

Role Title: Systems Architect / Chief Systems Architect

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote - US-based preferred; candidates with strong relevant experience worldwide considered.


micro1 is looking for experienced Systems Architects or Chief Systems Architects to support an AI training project focused on complex, real-world engineering workflows. In this role, you will draw on your experience defining system architectures and leading multidisciplinary engineering teams to design realistic tasks, coordinate contributions from domain experts, and establish clear technical objectives and evaluation criteria. Your expertise will help improve how AI systems reason about architecture, interfaces, dependencies, and engineering trade-offs.


Scope of Work

  1. Design realistic engineering projects requiring architectural decisions across multiple disciplines, such as mechanical, electrical, hardware, software, and manufacturing.
  2. Translate project objectives into system architectures with defined boundaries, subsystem responsibilities, interfaces, and technical constraints.
  3. Break complex architectural problems into connected tasks with defined inputs, deliverables, dependencies, and expert responsibilities.

Requirements

  1. Substantial professional experience as a Systems Architect, Chief Systems Architect, or in a comparable technical leadership role.
  2. Proven experience owning the architecture of complex engineering systems and leading multidisciplinary technical teams.
  3. Strong expertise in system architecture design, technical trade studies, interface management, and architecture reviews.
  4. English proficiency at B2 level or higher.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. A relevant master's degree or PhD in Systems Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.
  2. Experience with model-based systems engineering, SysML, or architecture modeling tools.
  3. Experience guiding system architectures from initial concept through implementation, integration, and deployment.
  4. Experience in aerospace, automotive, robotics, industrial systems, medical devices, or other complex engineering environments.

Role Title: Weapons Systems Operator


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is seeking current or former military Weapons Systems Operators to contribute to an AI development project focused on military operations, weapons employment, and tactical decision-making.   1. Evaluate AI-generated scenarios involving air defense, missile systems, naval weapons, or tactical aviation.

  1. Current or former military weapons systems operator with hands-on experience in air defense, missile operations, naval combat systems, or tactical aviation.

  3. Strong understanding of weapons employment, tactical decision-making, and military operational procedures.

  5. Operational deployments, live-fire experience, or experience as a weapons instructor are a plus.

Role Title: Corporate Transactions Attorney


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


We are seeking seasoned Corporate Transactions Attorneys for a part-time role at the forefront of legal AI. This opportunity is for elite lawyers who want to help shape how advanced AI is trained, evaluated, and applied in real-world legal work, especially those who have deep experience with drafting, reviewing, negotiating, and redlining within the tech field.


In this role, you will review, assess, and contribute to contract redlining workflows used to train and evaluate state-of-the-art AI models. Your work will directly improve how these systems identify risk and interpret contract language to create tools with improved precision and legal judgment.


Key Responsibilities:

  1. Perform simulated contract negotiations and redlining exercises.
  2. Review and assess AI responses to contract scenarios, providing expert feedback to improve model performance and output precision.
  3. Create objective evaluation frameworks and grading criteria to assess AI performance on contract tasks with rigor and consistency.
  4. Collaborate with product and research teams to refine data, guidelines, and best practices for AI-driven contract review solutions.


Required Skills and Qualifications:

  1. J.D. from an ABA-accredited law school.
  2. Active bar admission in at least one U.S. jurisdiction.
  3. Minimum of 2 years in the M&A department of a corporate law firm.
  4. Familiarity with standard M&A agreements, including APAs and SPAs.
  5. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with meticulous attention to detail.
  6. Strong analytical capabilities and ability to translate legal expertise into actionable feedback for AI systems.
  7. Demonstrated commitment to innovation at the intersection of law and technology.
  8. Experience working with cross-disciplinary teams in fast-paced environments.


Preferred Qualifications:

  1. Prior exposure to AI, legal tech, or training initiatives.
  2. Experience working with private equity firms.


Why Join:

  1. This is an opportunity to work at the intersection of law and technology.
  2. You will help define how AI is developed for a new generation of legal practitioners.
  3. You will apply your experience in a high-impact research environment.


Compensation Structure:


Compensation is task-based, meaning experts are paid per completed task that meets the project specifications. The average handling time (AHT) is approximately 3.5 hours per task, and the effective hourly rate will depend on the number of tasks completed and successfully signed off.
